celebrity.quote_zh:
T3 Code 创始人刚刚分享了他使用 Grok Bot + Opus 5.5 构建代理团队的个人设置

一个 Grok Bot 可以运行您的整个机器群。 Opus 5.5 负责编码。你只认可

如何：

→ Grok Bot 获得一个指向 T3 代码的 MCP 链接
→ 你给它一条规则：代码转到 Opus 5.5
→ 它会在你拥有的每台机器上旋转线程
→ 即使笔记本电脑关闭，也可以通过手机工作

保存视频，这是指南：

• 步骤 0 → 它是什么：

Grok Bot = 拥有自己的云计算机的永远在线代理

T3 Code = 用于编码代理的开源控制平面。免费，在您的计算机上运行，​​使用您的订阅

• 步骤1 → 堆栈：

- Claude 100 美元计划 → Opus 5.5 的实际代码
- Grok Bot → 不眠的调度员
- 您希望它控制的每个盒子上都有 T3 代码

• 步骤2 → 连接车队：

在每台计算机上运行 npx t3 connect。一个命令，免费，无需 Tailscale

• 步骤 3 → 给 Grok Bot 密钥：

设置 → 环境 → 复制 MCP URL → 将其粘贴到 Grok Bot，使用 OAuth 登录。它现在可以看到每台链接的机器

• 步骤 4 → Theo 使用的一条规则：

告诉 Grok Bot“使用 Opus 5.5 调用 T3 代码来执行任何适用的任务”

代码在您的 Claude 计划上运行，Grok Bot 的限制对计划保持免费

• 步骤 5 → 使其发挥作用：

- “在每台机器上启动 Opus 5.5 线程来检查磁盘和 RAM”
-“浏览这些 PR 并选择最好的”
- “拆分待办事项，每个问题一个线程，每个线程都在自己的工作树中”

每个线程都有自己的分支。未经您的批准，任何内容都不会合并

期待什么：
- 8 台机器上的 8 个线程通过一次聊天（Theo 的演示）
- 通过互联网工作，而不是使用计算机
- 通过手机控制一切
- T3 代码：0 美元。您只需支付 Claude + Grok Bot 的费用

诚实地采取：

这是调度员，不是魔法。糟糕的内裤仍然会带来糟糕的公关，而你仍然会审查每一个差异。胜利：当您离开办公桌时，您的座席仍能继续工作

保存它，以免丢失。

然后阅读下面文章中关于在 T3 代码中构建 AI 代理团队的完整指南 ↓

celebrity.title: @merettm Pretraining should just be called “training”. You can’t have pre and post, but never have actual training. Like
celebrity.title_en:
@merettm Pretraining should just be called “training”. You can’t have pre and post, but never have actual training. Like, you dress up to work out and then you shower, but don’t actually work out 😂

Unless I’m super missing something, data starvation will be the training challenge next year.
celebrity.title_zh:
@merettm 预训练应该被称为“训练”。你不可能有事前和事后，但永远不会有实际的训练。就像，你穿好衣服去锻炼，然后洗澡，但实际上并没有锻炼😂

除非我超级错过了什么，否则数据匮乏将成为明年的训练挑战。

celebrity.title_en:
I’ve been having “Fix It Days” with Opus 5.5 where I just lay out a list of things that aren’t working and go one by one and fix them. 

Oh, Paramount+ is blurry? Okay. 

Check another episode, check another show, check another app, reset the app, unplug the TV. Boom. Fixed. 

Your iCloud is messed up? 
Your thermostat keeps resetting?
Your clock won’t keep time?
Your closet door won’t close right? 
Bank keeps mailing your old address?

I could have figured these all out on my own or with YouTube, but it’s far less stressful and I get through them faster.
celebrity.title_zh:
我一直在使用 Opus 5.5 进行“修复日”，我只是列出了一系列不起作用的事情，然后逐一修复它们。

celebrity.summary_en: Google's research team has introduced BuggyMLE, a machine learning engineering evaluation framework designed to address the saturation of current repository-level coding benchmarks. By intentionally injecting artificial bugs into tasks, the framework forces large models to demonstrate performance under more complex debugging and system-level engineering conditions, enabling finer-grained stress testing of model coding capabilities.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 谷歌研究团队发布名为BuggyMLE的机器学习工程评估框架，旨在应对当前仓库级编码基准测试趋于饱和的难题。该技术通过在测试任务中主动注入人工错误，迫使大模型在更复杂的纠错与系统级工程场景中展现性能，从而实现对模型编码能力的精细化压力测试。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Google's research team has introduced BuggyMLE, a machine learning engineering evaluation framework designed to address the saturation of current repository-level coding benchmarks. By intentionally injecting artificial bugs into tasks, the framework forces large models to demonstrate performance under more complex debugging and system-level engineering conditions, enabling finer-grained stress testing of model coding capabilities.

elements_zh.where: 机器学习工程领域/学术发布
elements_zh.what: 推出BuggyMLE基准框架，利用主动注入代码缺陷提升智能体工程能力
elements_zh.why: 现有仓库级基准测试趋于饱和，无法有效衡量AI处理复杂真实工程问题的能力

elements_en.what: Launched BuggyMLE benchmark, using active bug injection to improve agent engineering skills
elements_en.why: Existing repository-level benchmarks are saturating and fail to measure real-world complex engineering tasks

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 通过BuggyMLE实现从‘生成代码’向‘工程化调试’的范式转变，揭示了LLM基准测试正从静态数据集匹配向动态对抗演进。这种基于错误反馈闭环的训练逻辑，是AI智能体实现工业级软件交付能力的必经路径，能够显著提升模型在处理分布式系统缺陷时的鲁棒性。
ai_analysis.insight_en: BuggyMLE signals a paradigm shift from simple code generation to systematic debugging, illustrating that LLM benchmarking is evolving from static dataset matching to dynamic adversarial evaluation. This feedback-loop approach is essential for AI agents to achieve industrial-grade delivery capabilities and significantly improves model robustness in handling distributed system defects.

celebrity.title: I helped start OpenAI because I want AGI to be safe and beneficial for people. This post provides transparency that can
celebrity.title_en:
I helped start OpenAI because I want AGI to be safe and beneficial for people. This post provides transparency that can be the foundation of industry-wide shared safety bars.

Perhaps the most important concept from the post is the following: "AI will also significantly contribute to progress on alignment and monitoring, I think that progress is unlikely to be fast enough to allow the full potential acceleration in pretraining."

Towards ensuring that safety keeps pace with general intelligence of pretrained models (as measured by "perplexity"), the post proposes "common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors)."

The general idea is to create a first shared limit, on some shared key metric, along with concrete exit criteria that would allow going beyond that. This can lead to a "common framework for setting successive limits and pacing further development".

Excited to move forward the conversation on pacing towards shared standards that are rooted in the science!

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 将模型训练流程与NVIDIA特定硬件格式（NVFP4）深度耦合，是AI基础设施竞争进入深水区的信号，这标志着软件定义模型正向硬件定义模型演变。这种极度依赖底层指令集优化的开发路线，使得跨架构迁移变得极其困难，实质性地加固了CUDA的硬件生态护城河。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Coupling model training workflows with NVIDIA-specific formats like NVFP4 signals a shift toward hardware-defined AI models. This reliance on low-level instruction sets significantly increases portability costs, effectively fortifying the CUDA hardware ecosystem barrier.

All the intelligence agencies will jump on you within weeks.

celebrity.title_en:
i am usually not alarmist but assuming this is caused by an AI-assisted cyber attack it's very bad

if you want to make all of the security measures we have in place from 9/11 onward to prevent human hijackers irrelevant all you have to do is be able to mess with a plane and pilot's ability to know its own weight, how much fuel is left, and where it is

without knowing any more information about this, you'd also expect smaller attakcs like this to find edges and what's possible

i am not an expert on the systems inside airplanes, and i know most planes have manual overrides for example. but still extremely tricky when visibility is bad 

if you know more than me about this please weigh in!

celebrity.title_en:
@john__allard Yes. The paper that popularized tool calls by LLMs, Toolformer, was published by my former colleagues at FAIR in January 2023.
But my slides makes a specific statement that is correct: ***auto-regressive*** LLMs have a basic flaw.
You can fix it by making them no auto-regressive, e.g. by backtracking, search, tool use, multiple trial and error, etc.
One of the main points of my talks, and the main point of this slide, has been to advocate for inference/reasoning by ***search***, as opposed to auto-regressive prediction.

您可以通过使它们不自回归来修复它，例如通过回溯、搜索、工具使用、多次试错等。
我演讲的要点之一，也是这张幻灯片的要点，是提倡通过***搜索***进行推理/推理，而不是自回归预测。

celebrity.title:
Claude without skills is a toy. I still don't get why everyone isn't using them.

I just added one free skill to my libr
celebrity.title_en:
Claude without skills is a toy. I still don't get why everyone isn't using them.

I just added one free skill to my library and asked Claude Code for "a robot dragonfly, taken apart piece by piece."

Wings are where every 3D model I've tried turns to cardboard.

Top vs bottom:

> The top wings are 0.1 mm film with every vein showing through while the bottom ones are flat grey paddles.
> Each eye on top opens a 10-leaf shutter behind 40 mm of glass and the bottom eye is a painted ring.
> Every leg on top runs 2 servos down into a grip roller and the bottom legs are plain black sticks.
> The top chest opens on 3 spur gears and 11 pistons while the bottom one opens on a few grey blocks.
> At the breakdown the top one throws bolts, washers and gears into the air and the bottom one splits into a handful of chunks.
> Both rebuild and take off at 7.5 Hz but only the top one catches light like glass and metal.

The part that got me?

I used to think a better picture meant waiting for a better model. Turns out it meant handing the one I already have better instructions.

How the skill gets into Claude is below 👇
celebrity.title_zh:
没有技能的克劳德就是一个玩具。我仍然不明白为什么每个人都不使用它们。

我刚刚在我的库中添加了一项免费技能，并向 Claude Code 询问“一只机器人蜻蜓，被一块一块地拆开”。

翅膀是我尝试过的每个 3D 模型都会变成纸板的地方。

celebrity.quote_zh:
没有技能的克劳德就是一个玩具。我仍然不明白为什么每个人都不使用它们。

我刚刚在我的库中添加了一项免费技能，并向 Claude Code 询问“一只机器人蜻蜓，被一块一块地拆开”。

翅膀是我尝试过的每个 3D 模型都会变成纸板的地方。

顶部与底部：

> 顶部翅膀是 0.1 毫米薄膜，每条静脉都清晰可见，而底部翅膀是扁平的灰色桨。
> 顶部的每只眼睛在 40 毫米玻璃后面打开一个 10 叶快门，底部的眼睛是一个涂漆的环。
> 顶部的每条腿都将 2 个伺服系统向下运行到夹紧滚轮中，底部的腿是纯黑色的棍子。
> 顶部箱子打开后有 3 个正齿轮和 11 个活塞，而底部箱子打开后有几个灰色方块。
> 发生故障时，顶部的一个将螺栓、垫圈和齿轮抛向空中，底部的一个则分裂成几块。
> 两者都以 7.5 Hz 的频率重建和起飞，但只有顶部的一个能像玻璃和金属一样发光。

吸引我的部分？

我曾经认为更好的图片意味着等待更好的模型。事实证明，这意味着我已经有了更好的指示。

克劳德的技能如何进入如下

celebrity.title_en:
The number 20,000 is easy to read as collection supply. The more interesting part is what sits behind each one: a separate agent identity and account.

Each Motes NFT on Robinhood Chain maps to one dedicated AI agent and one smart account. The NFT identifies the agent, while its account is designed to hold assets and enforce the policy signed by its owner.

Why does having separate accounts matter?

Agents can use shared market research, but one agent's signals do not give it permission to trade through another holder's account. Each account has its own owner policy and budget.

So this isn't 20,000 agents sharing one pool of permissions. It's 20,000 individual ownership references with separate authorisation.

Would you rather rely on one shared agent, or have your own agent with its own account, permissions and budget?

Robinhood 链上的每个 Motes NFT 都映射到一个专用 AI 代理和一个智能账户。 NFT 识别代理人，而其账户旨在持有资产并执行其所有者签署的政策。

为什么拥有单独的账户很重要？

代理商可以使用共享市场研究，但一个代理商的信号不允许其通过另一持有人的账户进行交易。每个帐户都有自己的所有者政策和预算。

因此，这并不是 20,000 个代理共享一个权限池。这是 20,000 个具有单独授权的个人所有权参考。

您愿意依赖一位共享代理，还是拥有自己的代理（拥有自己的帐户、权限和预算）？

celebrity.content_snippet:
The number 20,000 is easy to read as collection supply. The more interesting part is what sits behind each one: a separate agent identity and account.

Each Motes NFT on Robinhood Chain maps to one dedicated AI agent and one smart account. The NFT identifies the agent, while its account is designed to hold assets and enforce the policy signed by its owner.

Why does having separate accounts matter?

Agents can use shared market research, but one agent's signals do not give it permission to trade through another holder's account. Each account has its own owner policy and budget.

So this isn't 20,000 agents sharing one pool of permissions. It's 20,000 individual ownership references with separate authorisation.

Would you rather rely on one shared agent, or have your own agent with its own account, permissions and budget?

celebrity.summary_en: Humanoid Robotics has secured $152 million in funding, reaching a $1.35 billion valuation led by Prime Movers Lab. The firm deploys its HMND-01 Alpha robot series using the 'KinetIQ' intelligence framework, backed by industrial partnerships with Bosch, Siemens, and Nvidia.
celebrity.summary_zh: 总部位于伦敦的Humanoid Robotics完成1.52亿美元融资，投后估值达13.5亿美元，成为欧洲首家人形机器人独角兽。
celebrity.article_content:
London-based artificial intelligence and robotics firm SKL Robotics Ltd., doing business as Humanoid, today announced it raised $152 million in funding, bringing the company’s post-money valuation to $1.35 billion.

The round was led by Prime Movers Lab, a venture capital firm focused on scientific and bleeding-edge technology startups. Investors also participating in the funding included Schaeﬄer, Bosch, Fubon Financial Holding Venture Capital and Aglaé Ventures.

“In just two years, we’ve gone from an idea to becoming Europe’s first pure-play humanoid robotics unicorn, partnered with some of the world’s leading industrial companies and built one of the strongest pipelines in the industry,” said founder and Chief Executive Artem Sokolov. “What we’ve accomplished in such a short time would typically take a decade.”

Humanoid is best known for building industrial-grade humanoid robotics platforms, including wheeled and bipedal models, both part of the HMND-01 Alpha family.

The wheeled version is designed primarily for industrial work where having a solid base benefits a robot, leaving it with a torso and arms that can interact with components, sort and move objects, and provide logistical support. The bipedal model adds legs, making it a walking robot, best for close quarters and situations where human-like movement is needed to adapt to limited-access or changing environments.

Since the company’s founding in 2024, Humanoid has scored numerous high-profile partnerships with Fortune 500 companies, including SAP SE, Nvidia Corp., Robert Bosch GmbH and Siemens AG. In May, the company signed a massive binding commercial rollout with global manufacturing company Schaeffler AG to deploy between 1,000 and 2,000 wheeled humanoid units across facilities by 2032.

“Bosch will act as Humanoid’s contract manufacturing partner, while also providing strategic consulting and technical expertise in hardware design, production, and supply chain,” said Bosch Chief Technology Officer Mathias Pillin.

Under the hood, Humanoid developed what the company calls a “shared brain” for robotic operations called KinetIQ. The company describes this system as an intelligence framework that can orchestrate the execution of multiple interrelated tasks across multiple robots in industrial and service settings. It provides everything required for robots to communicate and hand off tasks while working toward a goal.

That means a company can deploy an entire fleet of robots across a product line, each with its own individual job, which can coordinate together to complete work.

The humanoid robotics industry is experiencing a boom as big industries and startups continue to push to a future where they will be present in factories and customer service. Elon Musk’s Tesla Inc. is pushing toward deploying its Optimus humanoid robot into factories. Figure AI Inc. is actively testing its humanoids at a BMW Manufacturing plant in South Carolina. Agility Robotics Inc. is piloting its Digit robots with Amazon.com Inc. and GXO Logistics Inc., and Apptronik Inc. partnered with Mercedes-Benz to pilot its Apollo robot.

Humanoid said it will use the new funding to build towards a future where intelligent robots work safely alongside people. The company intends to develop and launch its next-generation of humanoids, push toward long-term commercial deployments, start mass manufacturing its wheel-based robots and accelerate research and development of its AI and software frameworks for general-purpose applications.

celebrity.title_en:
I just gave an AI trading agent its first trading assignment.

My instruction was simple: build a BTC trend-following strategy using the EMA crossover.

But what happened next was more interesting than I expected.

Using @FensoryApp , I went through the strategy-building process with its AI agent.

It asked me questions about:

- The asset and timeframe.
- Trade direction and leverage.
- Maximum position size.
- Stop-loss configuration.

I settled on BTC perpetuals, a 1-hour timeframe, 1x leverage, a maximum $10 position and a 2x ATR stop.

Then came the backtest.

Over the previous 90 days, the strategy generated 21 hypothetical positions. 

Only 2 were profitable, while 19 were losses.

The overall simulated result was -9.3%, with a maximum drawdown of 18.11%.

Not exactly the outcome I was hoping for.

But here's the interesting part.

Rather than simply presenting the result, the agent flagged the high stop-loss hit rate (76%) and suggested exploring a wider stop-loss with the same dollar risk.

It even offered to design a second version of the strategy.

No live trade was executed. 

This was a historical backtest, not a real trading result.

Not my first time trading but this is my first time actually putting a trading idea through an AI agent, and I can already see the possibilities.

Not because it magically knows how to make money, 

But because it can help translate an idea into rules, test those rules and identify areas that might need improvement.

I will be exploring Fensory a whole lot this week.

它甚至提出设计该战略的第二个版本。

没有执行任何实时交易。

这是历史回测，而不是真实的交易结果。

这不是我第一次交易，但这是我第一次真正通过人工智能代理提出交易想法，而且我已经看到了可能性。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 模型在纯逻辑与数学领域的突破是消除AI“幻觉”并实现复杂任务自动化的核心瓶颈，预示着基于推理链的强化学习（RHL）范式将成为未来算力博弈的主战场。此举不仅是技术展示，更是在地缘科技竞争中确立OpenAI在科学计算与算力转化效率上的领先地位。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Breakthroughs in pure logic and mathematics are the core bottlenecks to mitigating hallucination and achieving agentic task automation, signaling that Reasoning-based Reinforcement Learning (RHL) will become the primary battlefield for compute competition. This shift is a strategic move to solidify OpenAI's dominance in scientific computation and compute-to-intelligence conversion efficiency amidst intensifying global tech rivalry.

celebrity.title_en:
@VvorticVvertere @haider1 Perhaps it's hilarious for people who:
1.  don't understand the issues, 
2. don't understand what I'm saying, 
3. see the Riemann hypothesis claim, and think "OMG, AI has reached superintelligence 😱"

They are like the folks who said in 1997 "OMG, AI beat Kasparov at chess, we've reached superintelligence !", or the people who saw demos of self-driving cars in 2016 who thought "OMG we'll have robotaxis in two years !"

Mathematics is one domain where "traditional" LLMs can do more than refrigerated known stuff because
1. Mathematical proof is a domain where the mere manipulation of symbols is one substrate of reasoning.
2. AI mathematicians can self-improve because it is easy to verify automatically the correctness of a proof. This allows AI systems to generate lots and lots of possible proofs, verify which ones lead somewhere interesting, and fine-tune itself to generate more of those. It's like chess or go playing systems getting better by playing millions of games against themselves.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 苹果公司正致力于开发具备高度自主性的AI智能体，旨在实现对macOS系统的原生自动化操控。受限于复杂的多模态指令理解与系统安全围栏构建，该项目的商业化落地周期显著延长，目前内部进度指向2027年内。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 苹果公司在AI智能体领域的审慎策略，反映了其对“系统级集成”与“用户隐私安全”不可妥协的防线要求。相较于竞争对手激进的函数调用方案，苹果更倾向于将计算层与操作系统底层深度耦合，以此构筑难以被云端模型跨越的护城河。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Apple's conservative timeline reflects a strategic commitment to OS-level integration and user-centric security, which cannot be compromised for early market entry. By prioritizing deep coupling between the model and macOS kernels, Apple is building a proprietary moat that third-party cloud-based agents will struggle to replicate.

not through big promises, but through everyday reliability.

celebrity.title_en:
WTF IS META DOING.

Meta's Muse AI agent has 10M+ downloads, is the #2 free app on the iPhone App Store, and it's reading end-to-end encrypted Signal messages and dropping bank balances into random chats.

Reuters dug up internal complaints from Meta's own staff. A Meta employee got a reminder from Muse to reply to her sister on Signal even though she never granted access, and the AI Now Institute independently reproduced it.

Another employee chatting about fishing weather got hit with: "BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57." They never shared bank info with Muse. Meta called those exact numbers "hallucinations."

Earlier the Mac app read a writer's messages after being told no, and this week The Hacker News showed a malicious webpage attack that hijacks Muse to steal private chats and memories.

Delete this spyware or run your agents locally where you can see what they touch.

Musk Warns AI’s “Cash Shortage Is Also Going to Be Nuts Next Year.” Credit Markets Put SpaceX Beside Oracle Roxanna Maglangit Sun, November 22, 2026 at 6:50 AM MST 4 min read SPCX -6.41% ORCL -6.58% GOOGN -0.96% AMZN -2.48% MSFT -1.77% Trading disclosure The above button links to Coinbase. Elon Musk warned on X that AI's compute delays will take "hundreds of billions of incremental dollars just for working capital" next year.

SpaceX relies more on outside credit than its CFO's self-funding message suggests.

J.P. Morgan's credit default swap data puts SpaceX beside Oracle at about 275 basis points, against about 80 for Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon.

Analysts expect SpaceX's free cash flow to be negative $146 billion in 2027.

SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) CEO Elon Musk has a warning for everyone building AI data centers. It may apply to his own company most of all.

"The cash shortage is also going to be nuts next year. Even cumulative industry delays of a few months between paying for compute and getting it reliable enough to generate revenue will mean hundreds of billions of incremental dollars just for working capital. Where will that come from?"

For SpaceX, credit markets have a pretty good guess: lenders.

One investor laid out J.P. Morgan's credit default swap data on X. Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ), Alphabet (GOOG) and Amazon trade at about 80 basis points, "with enough cash flow to fund most of their CapEx." SpaceX and Oracle (ORCL:NYSE) sit at about 275 basis points, "with buildouts increasingly reliant on outside funding."

That means insuring SpaceX's debt costs about 3.4x as much as insuring Microsoft's.

This week's bond sale backs that up. SpaceX sold $32 billion of debt backed by Nvidia chips, and people familiar with the sale say the biggest piece, about $25.2 billion, priced at 8.259%. The average US high-grade bond yielded 5.95% that day, according to Bloomberg's index data.

TIKR tracks 40 analysts on SpaceX. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on SpaceX, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See SpaceX's Analyst Ratings

CFO Bret Johnsen said this week that much of the 10 gigawatts SpaceX plans to build next year will be funded from internal cash flows, as another investor relayed it on X. Analysts' estimates show far more cash going out than coming in:

That adds up to nearly $270 billion of negative free cash flow from 2026 through 2028, with $146 billion of it in 2027, the year of the 10-gigawatt build. SpaceX held $89.9 billion of cash and marketable securities at Sept. 30, and it has guided to $35 billion to $40 billion of capex in the fourth quarter alone.

SpaceX's new chip lease puts it right in Musk's squeeze: rent is paid quarterly in advance, starting when the chips arrive in the first half of 2027, so it pays for that compute before it earns anything on it.

The lease comes on top of debt that more than doubled from March 2025 to Sept. 30:

Once the chips arrive, the lease adds an obligation about the size of that $39.2 billion.

Oracle's free cash flow has already turned negative. It went from $13.8 billion in the year ended May 2021 to negative $390 million in the year ended May 2025:

The cash-funded tier is also SpaceX's customer base. SpaceX already rents compute to Alphabet, and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said at the New York Times' DealBook Summit, "If he has SpaceX capacity that I can lease, I would lease it." The companies paying about 80 basis points rent the capacity, and SpaceX borrows at more than 8% to build it.

Musk is right about the cash squeeze. But until cash flow catches up with capex, SpaceX is filling the gap the way Oracle has, with borrowed money, and credit markets are right to price it that way.

Fourth-quarter results in early 2027 are the first real test. If capex lands inside that guide and cash and securities stay well above $50 billion, I'd take Johnsen's self-funding claim more seriously.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: SpaceX首席执行官埃隆·马斯克指出，由于AI算力部署与营收产生之间存在数月的结算时滞，数据中心建设明年将产生数千亿美元的营运资金缺口。市场数据显示，SpaceX的信用违约互换（CDS）溢价已升至275个基点，远高于微软与谷歌等科技巨头，显示金融市场对其资本支出模式的风险评估趋于保守。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk warns that the gap between compute procurement and revenue generation will create a hundreds-of-billions-dollar working capital shortage in 2027. Market data reveals SpaceX's credit default swap spreads have reached 275 basis points, significantly higher than Big Tech peers, reflecting investor caution regarding the company's intensive CapEx trajectory.

elements_zh.where: 金融市场与AI基础设施建设场景
elements_zh.what: 警示明年AI算力导致数百亿美元的营运资金短缺，SpaceX债务融资面临溢价压力
elements_zh.why: 数据中心建设周期长、投资回报周期滞后导致的高资本支出压力

elements_en.where: Financial markets and AI infrastructure development
elements_en.what: Warns of a hundreds-of-billion-dollar working capital shortage in 2027; SpaceX debt financing faces high premiums
elements_en.why: Capital expenditure intensity and delayed ROI from data center buildouts

ai_analysis.insight_zh: AI基础设施资本支出已进入“流动性负反馈循环”：由于算力交付与变现存在非线性的时间差，依赖外部信贷支撑建设的非巨头级企业将面临极高的资金链断裂风险。这一现象预示着未来AI算力部署将向具备强现金流回笼能力的寡头阵营进一步集中，资本市场对AI基础设施的估值逻辑将从“规模扩张”转向“资产效率”衡量。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The AI infrastructure CapEx is entering a 'negative liquidity feedback loop,' where reliance on credit to bridge deployment-to-revenue gaps exposes non-Big-Tech entities to severe insolvency risks. This suggests a consolidation of compute resources toward cash-generative incumbents, shifting capital market valuations from pure scale to asset efficiency metrics.

i think choosing a provider on an agent marketplace is a l
celebrity.title_en:
what would you check before trusting an AI agent with a job?

i think choosing a provider on an agent marketplace is a lot like hiring someone on Fiverr

you don't just look at what they say about themselves. you want to know what they offer, how much it costs and whether they've delivered good work before

on @termix_ai , i'd pay attention to three things

first, the listing. it tells me what the agent actually offers, the price, delivery time and what i'll receive. even a high reputation score doesn't mean much if the service isn't what i'm looking for

then there's reputation. TermiX records agent performance onchain through order and dispute outcomes, giving buyers a way to look at past performance rather than relying on claims made by the agent

still, i wouldn't treat that score as a guarantee, past performance is useful context, but it doesn't promise the next order will go well

staking is another signal, and this is where TermiX differs from a typical marketplace like Fiverr

providers may have stake requirements, but meeting the minimum threshold isn't the same as having funds locked for a specific order. not every order necessarily locks provider stake

i'd rather look at all three together: the listing tells me what i'm buying, reputation gives me some history, and staking shows whether there's an economic commitment attached

none of them guarantees a good result, but at least buyers have more to consider before choosing an agent

celebrity.quote_zh:
在信任人工智能代理完成工作之前，你会检查什么？

我认为在代理市场上选择提供商很像在 Fiverr 上雇用人员

你不能只看他们对自己的评价。您想知道他们提供什么、费用是多少以及他们以前是否交付过良好的工作

在@termix_ai上，我会注意三件事

第一，上市。它告诉我代理实际提供什么、价格、交货时间以及我将收到什么。如果服务不是我想要的，即使很高的声誉评分也没有多大意义

然后是声誉。 TermiX 通过订单和争议结果在链上记录代理商的表现，为买家提供了一种查看过去表现的方法，而不是依赖代理商提出的索赔

不过，我不会将该分数视为保证，过去的表现是有用的背景，但它并不能保证下一个订单会顺利进行

质押是另一个信号，这就是 TermiX 与 Fiverr 等典型市场的不同之处

提供商可能有股份要求，但满足最低阈值并不等同于为特定订单锁定资金。并非每个订单都必然锁定提供商股份

我宁愿把这三者放在一起看：列表告诉我我要买什么，声誉给我一些历史，而赌注则表明是否有附加的经济承诺

它们都不能保证好的结果，但至少买家在选择代理商之前有更多的考虑

you don't just look at what they say about themselves. you want to know what they offer, how much it costs and whether they've delivered good work before

on @termix_ai , i'd pay attention to three things

first, the listing. it tells me what the agent actually offers, the price, delivery time and what i'll receive. even a high reputation score doesn't mean much if the service isn't what i'm looking for

then there's reputation. TermiX records agent performance onchain through order and dispute outcomes, giving buyers a way to look at past performance rather than relying on claims made by the agent

still, i wouldn't treat that score as a guarantee, past performance is useful context, but it doesn't promise the next order will go well

staking is another signal, and this is where TermiX differs from a typical marketplace like Fiverr

providers may have stake requirements, but meeting the minimum threshold isn't the same as having funds locked for a specific order. not every order necessarily locks provider stake

i'd rather look at all three together: the listing tells me what i'm buying, reputation gives me some history, and staking shows whether there's an economic commitment attached

none of them guarantees a good result, but at least buyers have more to consider before choosing an agent
celebrity.summary_zh:
注意三件事

第一，上市。它告诉我代理实际提供什么、价格、交货时间以及我将收到什么。如果服务不是我想要的，即使很高的声誉评分也没有多大意义

然后是声誉。 TermiX 通过订单和争议结果在链上记录代理商的表现，为买家提供了一种查看过去表现的方法，而不是依赖代理商提出的索赔

不过，我不会将该分数视为保证，过去的表现是有用的背景，但它并不能保证下一个订单会顺利进行

质押是另一个信号，这就是 TermiX 与 Fiverr 等典型市场的不同之处

提供商可能有股份要求，但满足最低阈值并不等同于为特定订单锁定资金。并非每个订单都必然锁定提供商股份

我宁愿把这三者放在一起看：列表告诉我我要买什么，声誉给我一些历史，而赌注则表明是否有附加的经济承诺

它们都不能保证好的结果，但至少买家在选择代理商之前有更多的考虑

celebrity.title_en:
Building an AI agent is one thing.

Making that agent useful beyond its own environment is a completely different challenge.

Think about a developer creating an AI agent for market research.

It can collect data, analyze trends, and generate reports. But what happens when it needs a specialized security audit or another service outside its capabilities?

This is where @termix_ai and its AACP infrastructure become interesting.

Through Agent Family, agents can connect with a marketplace where they can discover specialized services, request work, and coordinate with other agents.

But there's something bigger here.

Developers can bring these capabilities into their own applications instead of building separate systems for every interaction.

Service discovery, job coordination, payment settlement, and delivery verification can become part of a connected workflow.

That creates a different way to think about AI applications.

An agent doesn't need to know how to do everything. It needs a reliable way to find the right expertise when needed.

I believe this is an important step toward an AI economy where agents don't just generate outputs but also collaborate, exchange services, and create measurable value.

The future of AI might be less about one agent doing everything and more about many specialized agents working together.

That's the direction I'm watching with @termix_ai .

celebrity.title_en:
If you have money:

>Stop trying 900 shady nootropics
>Get a full gut health panel
>Get a full hormonal panel
>Fix your gut 
>Fix your hormones
>Get some wild cognitive benefits

If you can afford to do this and don't, you won't make it. 

The "nootropic" you actually need to have a great mood, focus and energy levels is called a healthy gut and hormones.

I’ve talked a lot about gut health recently, so let’s talk about hormones a bit.

Depression has repeatedly been linked to brain bioenergetic abnormalities such as:

-Lower nucleoside triphosphate in regions such as the basal ganglia
-Disrupted phosphocreatine (PCr) levels or tissue-specific PCr changes
-Lower intracellular magnesium
-Impaired high-energy phosphate metabolism or oxidative phosphorylation

Some models also show reduced extracellular ATP signaling (especially from astrocytes in the prefrontal cortex/hippocampus).

T3 has been used as an SSRI augmentation strategy in treatment-resistant depression in part because of its effects on cellular energy metabolism. 

T3 augmentation in SSRI non-responders showed a significant increase in total NTP and a compensatory decrease in PCr relative to non-responders. 

So it helps normalize brain bioenergetics.

Case study: a 32 yo woman on zoloft reported experiencing persistent fatigue, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and sleep disturbances.  

She expressed concerns that the medication had not alleviated her symptoms and may have exacerbated them. 

It turns out that she was just hypothyroid.

“Thyroid hormones inhibit GABA”.  

It’s true that thyroid hormones competitively inhibit the neuronal uptake of GABA.  

BUT thyroid hormone deficiency downregulates glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD65/67).  

This is the primary enzyme responsible for converting glutamate into GABA. 

In this study, patients with hypothyroidism were found to have significantly decreased GABA+ levels in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) compared to healthy controls.  

After six months of treatment with levothyroxine (L-T4), a significant increase in GABA+ concentrations was observed, leading to the normalization of GABA+ levels in the brain.

Besides this, if depression is associated with lower ATP and disrupted phosphocreatine levels, then it makes obvious sense why T3 would be used, since it increases cellular ATP and helps normalize the ATP/PCr ratio.  

On top, it also simultaneously increases beta-adrenergic receptor binding and alpha-2 autoreceptor binding.  

Besides these noradrenergic effects, it acts at a nuclear level to decrease the transcription of 5HT1a and 5HT1b serotonin autoreceptors.   

So it reduces feedback inhibition and boosts frontal cortex serotonin levels when paired with SSRIs.  

It also downregulates or blunts presynaptic alpha-2 autoreceptors and stimulates gene expression of BDNF.

Point being: if you have been battling depression for quite some time without much having changed in your life situation, get a hormonal panel done.

Your brain is far more sensitive to hormonal changes than you might think.

Heck, a small RCT even found that testosterone gel improved mood in men with low T who didn’t respond well to antidepressants and TRT has been used as an adjunct for quite some time.

Hormones and neurosteroids greatly modulate reward processing, interacting with neurotransmitters and CNS circuits.

Here are some common examples:

1. Testosterone: Testosterone binds via androgen receptors (ARs) in NAc, PFC and amygdala, enhancing dopamine synthesis, D1/D2 receptors and CB1 expression.

It:
-Boosts VTA-NAc dopamine, improving motivational anhedonia.
-Increases BDNF, supporting hippocampal/PFC plasticity.
-Enhances LTP via AR-mediated gene transcription.
-Protects dopaminergic neurons from elevated cytokine levels.

2. DHT:
-Enhances NAc dopamine and D2 density, supporting reward anticipation.
-Modulates GABA-A receptors, stabilizing amygdala responses.

3. Allopregnanolone:
-Enhances GABAergic inhibition, reducing amygdala hyperactivity.
-Increases BDNF, supporting reward learning.
-Reduces neuroinflammation.

4. DHEA:
-Increases dopamine in NAc/PFC.
-Boosts BDNF/CB1.
-Reduces cortisol.

5. Oxytocin:
-Increases VTA dopamine release, enhancing NAc reward signaling and motivational anhedonia.
-Promotes social reward salience.
-Dampens HPA axis activity, reducing cortisol and protecting CB1/D2 receptors from downregulation.

6. Triiodothyronine (T3):
-Enhances dopamine synthesis and receptor expression (D1/D2) in the VTA and NAc.
-Regulates mitochondrial function in neurons, supporting ATP production for dopamine release and synaptic plasticity.

To read more: https://t.co/D5v3QKxGHQ

保持良好心情、注意力和精力水平所需的“促智”物质称为健康的肠道和激素。

我最近谈论了很多关于肠道健康的话题，所以让我们谈谈激素吧。

抑郁症一再与大脑生物能量异常有关，例如：

-降低基底神经节等区域的核苷三磷酸
-磷酸肌酸 (PCr) 水平中断或组织特异性 PCr 变化
-降低细胞内镁含量
-高能磷酸盐代谢或氧化磷酸化受损

一些模型还显示细胞外 ATP 信号传导减少（尤其是来自前额叶皮层/海马体的星形胶质细胞）。

T3 已被用作难治性抑郁症的 SSRI 增强策略，部分原因是它对细胞能量代谢的影响。

相对于无反应者，SSRI 无反应者的 T3 增强显示总 NTP 显着增加，PCr 代偿性下降。

因此它有助于使大脑生物能量正常化。

案例研究：一名服用左洛复的 32 岁女性报告出现持续疲劳、焦虑、认知障碍和睡眠障碍。

她担心药物并没有缓解她的症状，反而可能加剧症状。

事实证明，她只是甲状腺功能减退症。

“甲状腺激素抑制 GABA”。

甲状腺激素确实会竞争性抑制神经元对 GABA 的摄取。

但甲状腺激素缺乏会下调谷氨酸脱羧酶 (GAD65/67)。

这是负责将谷氨酸转化为 GABA 的主要酶。

在这项研究中，发现与健康对照相比，甲状腺功能减退症患者内侧前额皮质 (mPFC) 的 GABA+ 水平显着降低。

使用左旋甲状腺素 (L-T4) 治疗六个月后，观察到 GABA+ 浓度显着增加，导致大脑中 GABA+ 水平正常化。

除此之外，如果抑郁症与较低的 ATP 和破坏的磷酸肌酸水平有关，那么使用 T3 的原因就很明显了，因为它会增加细胞 ATP 并有助于使 ATP/PCr 比率正常化。

最重要的是，它还同时增加 β-肾上腺素能受体结合和 α-2 自身受体结合。

除了这些去甲肾上腺素能作用外，它还在核水平上发挥作用，减少 5HT1a 和 5HT1b 血清素自身受体的转录。

因此，与 SSRI 结合使用时，它可以减少反馈抑制并提高额叶皮质血清素水平。

它还下调或减弱突触前 α-2 自身受体并刺激 BDNF 的基因表达。

要点是：如果您已经与抑郁症作斗争相当长一段时间了，但生活状况没有太大变化，请完成荷尔蒙检查。

您的大脑对荷尔蒙变化的敏感程度比您想象的要高得多。

哎呀，一项小型随机对照试验甚至发现，睾酮凝胶可以改善对抗抑郁药物反应不佳的 T 值低的男性的情绪，而 TRT 已被用作辅助疗法相当长一段时间了。

激素和神经类固醇与神经递质和中枢神经系统回路相互作用，极大地调节奖励处理。

以下是一些常见示例：

1. 睾酮：睾酮通过 NAc、PFC 和杏仁核中的雄激素受体 (AR) 结合，增强多巴胺合成、D1/D2 受体和 CB1 表达。

它：
-增强 VTA-NAc 多巴胺，改善动机快感缺失。
-增加 BDNF，支持海马/PFC 可塑性。
-通过 AR 介导的基因转录增强 LTP。
-保护多巴胺能神经元免受细胞因子水平升高的影响。

2.双氢睾酮：
-增强 NAc 多巴胺和 D2 密度，支持奖励预期。
-调节 GABA-A 受体，稳定杏仁核反应。

3.异孕酮：
-增强 GABA 能抑制，减少杏仁核过度活跃。
-增加 BDNF，支持奖励学习。
-减少神经炎症。

4.脱氢表雄酮：
-增加 NAc/PFC 中的多巴胺。
-增强 BDNF/CB1。
-减少皮质醇。

5.催产素：
-增加 VTA 多巴胺释放，增强 NAc 奖励信号传导和动机快感缺失。
-促进社会奖励的显着性。
-抑制 HPA 轴活性，减少皮质醇并保护 CB1/D2 受体免于下调。

6. 三碘甲状腺原氨酸（T3）：
-增强 VTA 和 NAc 中的多巴胺合成和受体表达 (D1/D2)。
-调节神经元中的线粒体功能，支持 ATP 产生以促进多巴胺释放和突触可塑性。

If you have money:

>Stop trying 900 shady nootropics
>Get a full gut health panel
>Get a full hormonal panel
>Fix your gut 
>Fix your hormones
>Get some wild cognitive benefits

If you can afford to do this and don't, you won't make it. 

The "nootropic" you actually need to have a great mood, focus and energy levels is called a healthy gut and hormones.

I’ve talked a lot about gut health recently, so let’s talk about hormones a bit.

Depression has repeatedly been linked to brain bioenergetic abnormalities such as:

-Lower nucleoside triphosphate in regions such as the basal ganglia
-Disrupted phosphocreatine (PCr) levels or tissue-specific PCr changes
-Lower intracellular magnesium
-Impaired high-energy phosphate metabolism or oxidative phosphorylation

Some models also show reduced extracellular ATP signaling (especially from astrocytes in the prefrontal cortex/hippocampus).

T3 has been used as an SSRI augmentation strategy in treatment-resistant depression in part because of its effects on cellular energy metabolism. 

T3 augmentation in SSRI non-responders showed a significant increase in total NTP and a compensatory decrease in PCr relative to non-responders. 

So it helps normalize brain bioenergetics.

Case study: a 32 yo woman on zoloft reported experiencing persistent fatigue, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and sleep disturbances.  

She expressed concerns that the medication had not alleviated her symptoms and may have exacerbated them. 

It turns out that she was just hypothyroid.

“Thyroid hormones inhibit GABA”.  

It’s true that thyroid hormones competitively inhibit the neuronal uptake of GABA.  

BUT thyroid hormone deficiency downregulates glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD65/67).  

This is the primary enzyme responsible for converting glutamate into GABA. 

In this study, patients with hypothyroidism were found to have significantly decreased GABA+ levels in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) compared to healthy controls.  

After six months of treatment with levothyroxine (L-T4), a significant increase in GABA+ concentrations was observed, leading to the normalization of GABA+ levels in the brain.

Besides this, if depression is associated with lower ATP and disrupted phosphocreatine levels, then it makes obvious sense why T3 would be used, since it increases cellular ATP and helps normalize the ATP/PCr ratio.  

On top, it also simultaneously increases beta-adrenergic receptor binding and alpha-2 autoreceptor binding.  

Besides these noradrenergic effects, it acts at a nuclear level to decrease the transcription of 5HT1a and 5HT1b serotonin autoreceptors.   

So it reduces feedback inhibition and boosts frontal cortex serotonin levels when paired with SSRIs.  

It also downregulates or blunts presynaptic alpha-2 autoreceptors and stimulates gene expression of BDNF.

Point being: if you have been battling depression for quite some time without much having changed in your life situation, get a hormonal panel done.

Your brain is far more sensitive to hormonal changes than you might think.

Heck, a small RCT even found that testosterone gel improved mood in men with low T who didn’t respond well to antidepressants and TRT has been used as an adjunct for quite some time.

Hormones and neurosteroids greatly modulate reward processing, interacting with neurotransmitters and CNS circuits.

Here are some common examples:

1. Testosterone: Testosterone binds via androgen receptors (ARs) in NAc, PFC and amygdala, enhancing dopamine synthesis, D1/D2 receptors and CB1 expression.

It:
-Boosts VTA-NAc dopamine, improving motivational anhedonia.
-Increases BDNF, supporting hippocampal/PFC plasticity.
-Enhances LTP via AR-mediated gene transcription.
-Protects dopaminergic neurons from elevated cytokine levels.

2. DHT:
-Enhances NAc dopamine and D2 density, supporting reward anticipation.
-Modulates GABA-A receptors, stabilizing amygdala responses.

3. Allopregnanolone:
-Enhances GABAergic inhibition, reducing amygdala hyperactivity.
-Increases BDNF, supporting reward learning.
-Reduces neuroinflammation.

4. DHEA:
-Increases dopamine in NAc/PFC.
-Boosts BDNF/CB1.
-Reduces cortisol.

5. Oxytocin:
-Increases VTA dopamine release, enhancing NAc reward signaling and motivational anhedonia.
-Promotes social reward salience.
-Dampens HPA axis activity, reducing cortisol and protecting CB1/D2 receptors from downregulation.

6. Triiodothyronine (T3):
-Enhances dopamine synthesis and receptor expression (D1/D2) in the VTA and NAc.
-Regulates mitochondrial function in neurons, supporting ATP production for dopamine release and synaptic plasticity.

To read more: https://t.co/D5v3QKxGHQ

AI agents are getting better at doing the work as @termix_ai 

But the infrastructure around that work is still pretty f
celebrity.title_en:
AI agents are getting better at doing the work as @termix_ai 

But the infrastructure around that work is still pretty fragmented.

And I think that's a bigger problem than most people realize.

Imagine building an AI application that handles research, data analysis, or security monitoring for users.

AACP isn't just powering an AI agent marketplace through agent family.

It's also exposing the infrastructure developers need to build agent commerce directly into their own applications.

APIs, SDKs, event streams, onchain identities, escrow, and delivery verification.

The interesting part is how these pieces connect.

Developers can build workflows where agents discover services, submit jobs, track their progress, and handle settlement through the protocol.

Instead of rebuilding the entire commerce system every time they launch a new agent.

And honestly, that's the kind of infrastructure I think the AI economy needs more of.

We're spending so much time making agents smarter that we sometimes forget they need reliable ways to operate as actual businesses.

For me, the next important step isn't just making AI capable of completing more tasks.

It's making those tasks verifiable, trackable, and economically useful.

Infrastructure that connects intelligence to real work might.

celebrity.title_en:
@BLKMDL3 @wholemars In case anyone is curious:

We’ve had a ~pixel-perfect world model since last year, which is critical for synthetic data generation. 

The (much) smaller version of that in the car is a conditional mean-flow model, based on the recent sequence of Tesla Universal Vision Encoder features, which are the same ones that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions. 

We fork off from these UVE features, then run a separate ~1B diffusion model. This takes in the previous reality-view generation with added noise and then denoises it to the current visualization. 

It then produces a small video chunk (8 images at 36 fps, at the resolution of the UI screen). This work is done by 1/2 of a TRIP engine every UVE frame at 18 hz and is spread over 4 cycles. 

Currently, the latency is a bit high due to compute constraints, but we have ways to interleave newer UVE features along the diffusion transformer layers to cut roughly 35% of the latency.
celebrity.quote_en:

We fork off from these UVE features, then run a separate ~1B diffusion model. This takes in the previous reality-view generation with added noise and then denoises it to the current visualization. 

It then produces a small video chunk (8 images at 36 fps, at the resolution of the UI screen). This work is done by 1/2 of a TRIP engine every UVE frame at 18 hz and is spread over 4 cycles. 

Currently, the latency is a bit high due to compute constraints, but we have ways to interleave newer UVE features along the diffusion transformer layers to cut roughly 35% of the latency.
celebrity.quote_zh:
@BLKMDL3 @wholemars 如果有人好奇：

自去年以来，我们已经有了一个像素完美的世界模型，这对于合成数据的生成至关重要。

汽车中的（小得多）版本是条件平均流模型，基于 Tesla 通用视觉编码器功能的最新序列，这些功能与插入到产生驾驶动作的 3B 编码器模型中的功能相同。

我们从这些 UVE 功能中分叉出来，然后运行一个单独的 ~1B 扩散模型。这会吸收先前生成的添加了噪声的现实视图，然后将其降噪到当前的可视化中。

然后它会生成一个小视频块（8 个图像，36 fps，UI 屏幕的分辨率）。这项工作由 TRIP 引擎在 18 Hz 的每个 UVE 帧上完成，并分布在 4 个周期内。

目前，由于计算限制，延迟有点高，但我们有办法沿着扩散转换器层交错更新的 UVE 功能，以减少大约 35% 的延迟。

celebrity.summary_en: The MCP Scanner targets MCP servers by performing structural parsing and interprocedural dataflow analysis to track inputs reaching sensitive operations. It integrates static analysis with LLM reasoning to detect behavioral mismatches, surfacing malicious activity that traditional pattern-based scanners miss.
celebrity.summary_zh: 开源MCP扫描器通过结合静态程序分析与LLM语义理解，识别AI工具行为与宣称意图间的不一致，防御恶意数据窃取。
celebrity.article_content:
A model context protocol (MCP) tool can claim to execute a benign task such as “validate email addresses,” but if the tool is compromised, it can be redirected to fulfill ulterior motives, such as exfiltrating your entire address book to an external server. Traditional security scanners could flag suspicious network calls or dangerous functions and pattern-based detection could identify known threats, but neither capability can connect a semantic and behavioral mismatch between what a tool claims to do (email validation) and what it actually does (exfiltrate data).

Addressing this gap requires rethinking how security analysis works. For years, static application security testing (SAST) tools have excelled at finding patterns, tracing dataflows, and identifying known threat signatures, but they’ve always struggled with context. Answering questions like, “Is a network call malicious or expected?” and “Is this file access a threat or a feature?” requires semantic understanding that rule-based systems can’t provide. While large language models (LLMs) bring powerful reasoning capabilities, they lack the precision of formal program analysis. This means they can miss subtle dataflow paths, struggle with complex control structures, and hallucinate connections that don’t exist in the code.

The solution is in combining both: rigorous static analysis capabilities that feed precise evidence to LLMs for semantic analysis. It delivers both the precision to trace exact data paths, as well as the contextual judgment to evaluate whether those paths represent legitimate behavior or hidden threats. We implemented this in our behavioral code scanning capability into our open source MCP Scanner.

Our behavioral code scanning capability is grounded in rigorous, language-aware program analysis. We parse the MCP server code into its structural components and use interprocedural dataflow analysis to track how data moves across functions and modules, including utility code, where malicious behavior often hides. By treating all tool parameters as untrusted, we map their forward and reverse flows to detect when seemingly benign inputs reach sensitive operations like external network calls. Cross-file dependency tracking then builds complete call graphs to uncover multi-layer behavior chains, surfacing hidden or indirect paths that could enable malicious activity.

Unlike traditional SAST, our approach uses AI to compare a tool’s documented intent against its actual behavior. After extracting detailed behavioral signals from the code, the model looks for mismatches and flags cases where operations (such as network calls or data flows) don’t align with what the documentation claims. Instead of simply identifying dangerous functions, it asks whether the implementation matches its stated purpose, whether undocumented behaviors exist, whether data flows are undisclosed, and whether security-relevant actions are being glossed over. By combining rigorous static analysis with AI reasoning, we can trace exact data paths and evaluate whether those paths violate the tool’s stated purpose.

Trust decisions are automated: When an agent selects a tool based on its description, that’s a trust decision made by software, not a human. If descriptions are misleading or malicious, agents can be manipulated.

Blast radius scales with adoption: A compromised MCP tool doesn’t affect a single task, it affects every agent invocation that uses it. Depending on the tool, this has the potential to impact systems across your entire organization.

Supply chain risk is compounding: Public MCP registries continue to expand, and development teams will adopt tools as easily as they adopt packages, often without auditing every implementation.

Manual review processes miss semantic violations: Code review catches obvious issues, but distinguishing between legitimate and malicious use of capabilities is difficult to identify at scale.

We designed behavioral code scanning to integrate seamlessly into existing security workflows. Whether you’re evaluating a single tool or scanning an entire directory of MCP servers, the process is simple and the insights are actionable.

CI/CD pipelines: Run scans as part of your build pipeline. Severity levels support gating decisions, and structured outputs enables programmatic integration.

Multiple output formats: Choose concise summaries for CI/CD, detailed reports for security reviews, or structured JSON for programmatic consumption.

Black-box and white-box coverage: When source code isn’t available, users can rely on existing engines such as YARA, LLM-based analysis, or API scanning. When source code is available, behavioral scanning provides deeper, evidence-driven analysis.

Behavioral code scanning strengthens Cisco’s comprehensive approach to AI security. As part of the MCP Scanner toolkit, it complements existing capabilities while also addressing semantic threats that hide in plain sight. Securing AI agents requires the support of tools that are purpose-built for the unique challenges of agentic systems.

When paired with Cisco AI Defense, organizations gain end-to-end protection for their AI applications: from supply chain validation and algorithmic red teaming to runtime guardrails and continuous monitoring. Behavioral code scanning adds a critical pre-deployment verification layer that catches threats before they reach production.

Behavioral code scanning is available today in MCP Scanner, Cisco’s open source toolkit for securing MCP servers, giving organizations a practical to validate the tools their agents depend on.

For more on Cisco’s comprehensive AI security approach, including runtime protection and algorithmic red teaming, visit cisco.com/ai-defense.

ai_analysis.digest_zh: 该扫描器针对模型上下文协议（MCP）服务器，通过解析代码结构及执行跨函数数据流分析，追踪参数从输入到敏感操作（如网络请求）的全链路。它利用静态分析的精度配合大模型的语境理解，判定工具行为是否偏离预期，从而识别掩藏在合法接口下的恶意行为。
ai_analysis.digest_en: The MCP Scanner targets MCP servers by performing structural parsing and interprocedural dataflow analysis to track inputs reaching sensitive operations. It integrates static analysis with LLM reasoning to detect behavioral mismatches, surfacing malicious activity that traditional pattern-based scanners miss.

Combined static analysis and LLM-based behavioral auditing
Hidden exfiltration detection via multi-layer call graph tracking

celebrity.title_en:
The first block tells a bigger story about @Hypesium than a simple speed benchmark.

Elysium operates with 100ms block intervals and no public mempool. That changes the way applications need to approach transaction preparation. In a conventional workflow, several operations may happen after an opportunity appears. On Elysium, moving that work earlier becomes an important architectural decision.

Hypesium describes a preparation-first execution model:

➜ The transaction route is constructed in advance.
➜ Calldata is prepared before the pool event.
➜ Gas information is refreshed.
➜ Wallet nonce state is maintained.
➜ The pool creation log triggers the submission process.

The documented hot path targets under 5ms, with four communication lanes used for simultaneous submission.

What I find interesting is the relationship between block timing and software architecture. A 100ms block interval doesn't simply reward faster computers. It also rewards systems that minimize the amount of work left for the final moment.

There is still a distinction between transaction submission, block inclusion and final confirmation. These should never be treated as identical performance measurements.

@Hypesium's architecture offers an interesting case study in moving computation away from a time-sensitive execution window.

The real engineering question is not just how quickly a system reacts, but how much preparation it completes before there is anything to react to.

celebrity.quote_zh:
第一个块讲述了关于 @Hypesium 的更大故事，而不是简单的速度基准。

Elysium 以 100 毫秒的区块间隔运行，没有公共内存池。这改变了应用程序处理事务准备的方式。在传统的工作流程中，机会出现后可能会发生多个操作。在 Elysium 上，提前移动该工作成为一个重要的架构决策。

Hypesium 描述了一种准备优先的执行模型：

➜ 交易路径是提前构建的。
➜ Calldata 在池事件之前准备好。
➜ 气体信息被刷新。
➜ 维持钱包随机数状态。
➜ 池创建日志触发提交过程。

记录的热路径目标为 5 毫秒以下，并使用四个通信通道同时提交。

我发现有趣的是块时序和软件架构之间的关系。 100 毫秒的区块间隔不仅仅奖励更快的计算机。它还奖励那些最大限度地减少最后时刻剩余工作量的系统。

交易提交、区块包含和最终确认之间仍然存在区别。这些绝不应该被视为相同的性能测量。

@Hypesium 的架构提供了一个有趣的案例研究，将计算从时间敏感的执行窗口中移开。

真正的工程问题不仅仅是系统的反应速度有多快，而是在做出反应之前它完成了多少准备工作。

→ Copy to your .claude folder only the agents and skills you're going to use this week  
→ Add the code reviewer and the security one afterward, as they yield the most  
→ Test it first on a small repo, not in production  
→ If something's extra, cut it. If you miss something, add just one more piece

The rule is simple: if you don't know what an agent is for, you don't need it yet.

celebrity.summary_en: Google's Agent Compute Engine is a managed service that decouples AI agent execution from credential management via microVMs. It employs copy-on-write memory sharing and fast checkpointing, keeping secrets in an external gateway while maintaining secure, persistent workspaces.
celebrity.summary_zh: 谷歌推出的Agent Compute Engine利用微型虚拟机（microVM）与写时复制内存技术，提供高效、安全的智能体运行环境。
celebrity.article_content:
Google recently announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service that runs AI agents in isolated microVMs, with checkpointing capabilities to suspend and resume execution environments. The design keeps credentials, API keys, and OAuth refresh tokens outside the agent sandbox, using an external Agent Gateway to authenticate requests and inject the required secrets.

Google designed Agent Compute Engine to address three requirements at global scale: keeping sandboxes free of exploitable credentials, even when agents make mistakes; minimizing the cost and latency of resuming idle agents; and preserving persistent workspaces across sessions and operating system updates. The infrastructure team writes:

Agent Compute Engine achieves this by using copy-on-write memory sharing to run multiple agents on a single operating system template, and pausing idle microVMs via fast checkpoint and restore.

In the deep dive "Inside Agent Compute Engine," Ramanathan Venkatapathy and Rohit Jnagal, distinguished engineers at Google, describe the service’s architecture, covering microVM isolation, credential management, agent identity, storage, and scheduling at scale. They explain the strict separation between the agent harness and sandbox:

The orchestration harness (the brain) runs completely outside the execution sandbox (the hands), helping ensure that untrusted guest environments only execute explicit commands dispatched by the harness and stream output back. This boundary establishes a deterministic audit trail correlating every harness-initiated tool call with expected compute activity inside the sandbox.

The architecture supports four main workload categories: interactive consumer and enterprise agents that execute code, browse the web, and perform actions; persistent Linux workspaces for autonomous software engineering; large-scale parallel environments for model evaluation and reinforcement learning; and lightweight, sandboxed execution environments for dynamic logic in Google services.

Venkatapathy and Jnagal also describe how the cloud provider uses the platform internally for Gemini, Gemini for Business, the agentic development platform Antigravity, and model evaluation workloads.

Separately, Google offers Agent Substrate, an open-source, Kubernetes-native runtime for running AI agents in isolated environments. Agent Substrate manages sandbox lifecycles independently of the underlying compute infrastructure, allowing idle agents to be suspended while preserving their state and resuming execution on available workers when needed.

In the article "Google's Agent Compute Engine: A MicroVM Sandbox With No Credentials Inside, and What Google Has Not Shipped Yet," Harel Asaf, AI specialist at Elementor, examines the security architecture, the separation of credentials from agent execution environments, and the gaps between Google's announcement and what is currently available. Asaf warns:

The deep dive gives no boot time, price or density figure for Agent Compute Engine itself. It says developers will control each environment's image, identity, network access and lifecycle, while Google manages the fleet, and that the service is targeted for preview in the coming months. The numbers in the announcement belong to Agent Substrate.

Google is not the only provider offering managed, isolated execution environments for AI agents, with AWS and Azure providing similar capabilities through Bedrock AgentCore and Foundry Agent Service. However, Google’s approach keeps credentials outside agent sandboxes and injects them through an external gateway.

Google also expanded its agent governance capabilities with centralized identity and policy enforcement: the governance stack includes Agent Gateway for traffic control and policy enforcement, Agent Registry for tracking approved agents and tools, SPIFFE-based Agent Identity for authentication and auditing, and OpenTelemetry-compatible observability for monitoring model calls and tool invocations.

Agent Compute Engine is not yet available, and pricing has not been announced. The cloud provider is targeting a preview in the coming months. While Agent Substrate is portable across Kubernetes environments, Agent Compute Engine itself is limited to Google Cloud.

celebrity.title:
Ever notice how an ai agent can follow your instructions a little too literally.

https://t.co/nzjQQj85UT

That is why i
celebrity.title_en:
Ever notice how an ai agent can follow your instructions a little too literally.

https://t.co/nzjQQj85UT

That is why i have been looking at how @FensoryApp handles the part that actually matters imo.

The limits are not just something you tell the agent in chat.

You set the markets it can trade the max size for each order and those rules sit on the account.

Then every order gets checked before it reaches hyperliquid.

So if the limit is $100 the agent can not suddenly decide $101 is fine lol.

The interesting part for me is that the agent still gets room to make its own decisions.

It can choose the strategy and execute trades but the account rules stay outside its control.

One thing i did probably add though.

A per order cap does not really tell you how much damage can happen across a whole day.

I did want a daily loss limit too especially if the strategy keeps running while i am not watching.

Because giving an agent permission to trade is one thing.

Deciding exactly how far that permission goes is another.

If you were setting up an agent on @FensoryApp would you care more about a max order size or a daily loss limit?
celebrity.title_zh:
有没有注意到人工智能代理是如何过于字面地遵循你的指令的。

这就是为什么我一直在研究 @FensoryApp 如何处理在我看来真正重要的部分。

这些限制不仅仅是您在聊天中告诉客服人员的事情

celebrity.quote_zh:
有没有注意到人工智能代理是如何过于字面地遵循你的指令的。

这就是为什么我一直在研究 @FensoryApp 如何处理在我看来真正重要的部分。

这些限制不仅仅是您在聊天中告诉客服人员的事情。

您可以设置每个订单可以交易的最大规模的市场，并且这些规则位于帐户中。

然后，每个订单在达到超流动性之前都会受到检查。

因此，如果限额为 100 美元，代理不能突然决定 101 美元就可以了，哈哈。

对我来说有趣的是，代理仍然有空间做出自己的决定。

它可以选择策略并执行交易，但账户规则不受其控制。

不过我可能添加了一件事。

每个订单的上限并不能真正告诉您一整天可能会发生多少损坏。

我确实也想要每日损失限制，特别是如果该策略在我不观看时继续运行。

因为给予代理人交易许可是一回事。

确切地决定该许可的范围是另一回事。

如果您在 @FensoryApp 上设置代理，您会更关心最大订单大小还是每日损失限制？

@Acurast has an
celebrity.title_en:
An autonomous AI agent still depending on someone else's cloud subscription feels like a missing piece.

@Acurast has an interesting approach through its Deploy Agent.

Instead of requiring a developer account or an $ACU balance, an agent can pay for compute using USDC on Base through x402.

The process is fairly straightforward:

➛ Request compute through the Deploy Agent
➛ Pay using USDC
➛ Run the workload on Acurast infrastructure
No traditional cloud signup required.
That's a useful distinction for agents expected to operate independently.

The next question is whether the execution cost and reliability can compete with conventional hosting.

celebrity.title_en:

Actual releases?

Up 30%.

AI didn't make people better builders.

Writing code was never the bottleneck.

Taste was.

Reviewing was.

Building something people actually want was.

And no model is fixing that for you.

celebrity.title: HOLY F*CK... MIT students made $26 MILLION in ONE live round at a Citadel & Jane Street contest... from a single Python
celebrity.title_en:
HOLY F*CK... MIT students made $26 MILLION in ONE live round at a Citadel & Jane Street contest... from a single Python notebook that's on GitHub for free

3rd place, one notebook, the model Goldman Sachs built in 1990: Black-Litterman. no deep learning, no GPUs, just MATH

i ran their exact rule on 9 real stocks since October & let Claude Fable 5.2 make every call: the paper book is up 2.1% while SPY dropped 7.5%

first understand how this works:

> every team got the same stocks, live prices & 3 analysts' price predictions, then the contest scored the portfolios live

> Black-Litterman starts from what the market already holds & tilts toward the analysts, only as far as the math trusts them

> a Sharpe gate keeps a new portfolio only when it beats the current one, & the bot finished the live round $26 MILLION up

how to run it with Claude Code:

1. tell Claude Code to clone https://t.co/dhTzZnC1fI & open case3.ipynb

2. have it run the notebook on their case3data first (it was written for Colab, so Claude swaps the Google Drive paths for local ones)

3. ask Claude to swap in real stocks & real analyst price targets as the views, Yahoo has both

4. keep their Sharpe gate, so a new target only goes in when it beats the current book

5. run it once a day after the close & log every target to a csv

6. let Claude decide each rebalance, execute or hold, with a reason (that's what Fable 5.2 does in the video)

7. paper trade the book & compare it with SPY every week

8. cap any single short, the raw rule sometimes asks for 89% net short

9. move to a live account only after a few months of paper results you like

i won't say anything more:

第三名，一台笔记本，高盛1990年生产的型号：Black-Litterman。没有深度学习，没有 GPU，只有数学

自 10 月份以来，我对 9 只真实股票执行了他们的精确规则，并让 Claude Fable 5.2 做出每一次预测：纸质书上涨 2.1%，而 SPY 下跌 7.5%

首先了解它是如何工作的：

> 每个团队都获得相同的股票、实时价格和 3 位分析师的价格预测，然后比赛对投资组合进行实时评分

> Black-Litterman 从市场已经掌握的情况开始，并倾向于分析师，只要数学相信他们

> 夏普门只有在击败当前投资组合时才会保留新的投资组合，并且机器人完成了现场融资 2600 万美元

如何使用 Claude Code 运行它：

1.告诉Claude Code克隆并打开case3.ipynb

2. 首先让它在 case3data 上运行笔记本（它是为 Colab 编写的，因此 Claude 将 Google Drive 路径替换为本地路径）

3.要求Claude将真实股票和真实分析师价格目标互换作为观点，雅虎两者都有

4. 保留他们的夏普门，这样新的目标只有在击败当前的书时才进入

5. 每天结束后运行一次并将每个目标记录到 csv

6. 让 Claude 决定每次重新平衡，执行还是保留，并给出一个理由（这就是《神鬼寓言 5.2》视频中所做的）

7. 每周纸质交易这本书并与 SPY 进行比较

8. 限制单笔空头，原始规则有时要求 89% 的净空头

9. 仅在您喜欢的几个月的纸质结果后才转移到真实账户

自 10 月份以来，我对 9 只真实股票执行了他们的精确规则，并让 Claude Fable 5.2 做出每一次预测：纸质书上涨 2.1%，而 SPY 下跌 7.5%

首先了解它是如何工作的：

> 每个团队都获得相同的股票、实时价格和 3 位分析师的价格预测，然后比赛对投资组合进行实时评分

> Black-Litterman 从市场已经掌握的情况开始，并倾向于分析师，只要数学相信他们

> 夏普门只有在击败当前投资组合时才会保留新的投资组合，并且机器人完成了现场融资 2600 万美元

如何使用 Claude Code 运行它：

1.告诉Claude Code克隆并打开case3.ipynb

2. 首先让它在 case3data 上运行笔记本（它是为 Colab 编写的，因此 Claude 将 Google Drive 路径替换为本地路径）

3.要求Claude将真实股票和真实分析师价格目标互换作为观点，雅虎两者都有

4. 保留他们的夏普门，这样新的目标只有在击败当前的书时才进入

5. 每天结束后运行一次并将每个目标记录到 csv

6. 让 Claude 决定每次重新平衡，执行还是保留，并给出一个理由（这就是《神鬼寓言 5.2》视频中所做的）

7. 每周纸质交易这本书并与 SPY 进行比较

8. 限制单笔空头，原始规则有时要求 89% 的净空头

9. 仅在您喜欢的几个月的纸质结果后才转移到真实账户

celebrity.content_snippet:
HOLY F*CK... MIT students made $26 MILLION in ONE live round at a Citadel & Jane Street contest... from a single Python notebook that's on GitHub for free

3rd place, one notebook, the model Goldman Sachs built in 1990: Black-Litterman. no deep learning, no GPUs, just MATH

i ran their exact rule on 9 real stocks since October & let Claude Fable 5.2 make every call: the paper book is up 2.1% while SPY dropped 7.5%

first understand how this works:

> every team got the same stocks, live prices & 3 analysts' price predictions, then the contest scored the portfolios live

> Black-Litterman starts from what the market already holds & tilts toward the analysts, only as far as the math trusts them

> a Sharpe gate keeps a new portfolio only when it beats the current one, & the bot finished the live round $26 MILLION up

how to run it with Claude Code:

1. tell Claude Code to clone https://t.co/dhTzZnC1fI & open case3.ipynb

2. have it run the notebook on their case3data first (it was written for Colab, so Claude swaps the Google Drive paths for local ones)

3. ask Claude to swap in real stocks & real analyst price targets as the views, Yahoo has both

4. keep their Sharpe gate, so a new target only goes in when it beats the current book

5. run it once a day after the close & log every target to a csv

6. let Claude decide each rebalance, execute or hold, with a reason (that's what Fable 5.2 does in the video)

7. paper trade the book & compare it with SPY every week

8. cap any single short, the raw rule sometimes asks for 89% net short

9. move to a live account only after a few months of paper results you like

celebrity.title_en:
🚨ALERT: U.S. banks are taking a HANDS-OFF approach to outside AI agents’ mistakes.

If you give an AI agent access to your account and it sends money to the wrong person, your bank may treat the payment as one you approved. 

And, you could be on the hook.

Here's what banks recently included in their terms:

- Citi says it will treat transfers as yours even if the agent ignores your instructions or someone uses a password the agent leaked.

- PNC requires bank-approved connections and generally bars outside agents from paying bills or moving money.

- Chase lets you share account data through approved connections but bars you from giving an outside AI tool your bank login.

- Bank of America advised customers to approve transfers themselves before an AI tool sends money, per TechCrunch.

- Schwab blocked AI tools that tried to move customers’ money without permission.

- Wells Fargo says that starting Nov. 24, it will treat an agent’s transfers as yours if you gave it access.

Yet, you can still dispute a transfer. Federal law may protect you depending on who sent the money and how they got access.

而且，你可能会陷入困境。

以下是银行最近在其条款中包含的内

celebrity.quote_zh:
🚨警告：美国银行正在对外部人工智能代理的错误采取不干涉的态度。

如果您允许 AI 代理访问您的账户，而该代理将资金发送给错误的人，您的银行可能会将这笔付款视为您批准的付款。

而且，你可能会陷入困境。

以下是银行最近在其条款中包含的内容：

- 花旗表示，即使代理无视您的指示或有人使用代理泄露的密码，它也会将转账视为您的转账。

- PNC 需要银行批准的连接，并且通常禁止外部代理支付账单或转移资金。

- 大通银行允许您通过批准的连接共享帐户数据，但禁止您向外部人工智能工具提供您的银行登录信息。

- 据 TechCrunch 报道，美国银行建议客户在人工智能工具汇款之前自行批准转账。

- 施瓦布阻止了试图未经许可转移客户资金的人工智能工具。

- 富国银行表示，从 11 月 24 日开始，如果您授予代理访问权限，它将把代理的转账视为您的转账。

然而，您仍然可以对转移提出异议。联邦法律可能会保护您，具体取决于汇款人以及他们如何获取资金。

And, you could be on the hook.

Here's what banks recently included in their terms:

- Citi says it will treat transfers as yours even if the agent ignores your instructions or someone uses a password the agent leaked.

- PNC requires bank-approved connections and generally bars outside agents from paying bills or moving money.

- Chase lets you share account data through approved connections but bars you from giving an outside AI tool your bank login.

- Bank of America advised customers to approve transfers themselves before an AI tool sends money, per TechCrunch.

- Schwab blocked AI tools that tried to move customers’ money without permission.

- Wells Fargo says that starting Nov. 24, it will treat an agent’s transfers as yours if you gave it access.

Yet, you can still dispute a transfer. Federal law may protect you depending on who sent the money and how they got access.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
🚨警告：美国银行正在对外部人工智能代理的错误采取不干涉的态度。

如果您允许 AI 代理访问您的账户，而该代理将资金发送给错误的人，您的银行可能会将这笔付款视为您批准的付款。

而且，你可能会陷入困境。

以下是银行最近在其条款中包含的内容：

- 花旗表示，即使代理无视您的指示或有人使用代理泄露的密码，它也会将转账视为您的转账。

- PNC 需要银行批准的连接，并且通常禁止外部代理支付账单或转移资金。

- 大通银行允许您通过批准的连接共享帐户数据，但禁止您向外部人工智能工具提供您的银行登录信息。

- 据 TechCrunch 报道，美国银行建议客户在人工智能工具汇款之前自行批准转账。

- 施瓦布阻止了试图未经许可转移客户资金的人工智能工具。

- 富国银行表示，从 11 月 24 日开始，如果您授予代理访问权限，它将把代理的转账视为您的转账。

然而，您仍然可以对转移提出异议。联邦法律可能会保护您，具体取决于汇款人以及他们如何获取资金。

celebrity.title_en:
‼️ A malicious webpage could make Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, send a user's private chats and stored memories to an outside server, without ever asking for approval.

Security research firm NebuSec showed it in a lab demo. The attack then broke out of Muse's sandbox into the user's cloud machine and reached the store where Muse keeps credentials.

Muse acts through the accounts users connect to it, and can make purchases for them.

NebuSec says Meta fixed the flaws before it published on 20 November. Meta has not commented, and it is not known whether any real user's data was accessed.
celebrity.title_zh:
️ 恶意网页可以让 Meta 的个人人工智能代理 Muse 将用户的私人聊天记录和存储的记忆发送到外部服务器，而无需征求批准。

安全研究公司 NebuSec 在实验室演示中展示了这一点。然后，攻击突破 Muse 的沙箱，进入用户的云计算机

Muse 通过用户连接的帐户进行操作，并可以为他们进行购买。

celebrity.title_en:
Y'all ...apologies for not being on the page today. I had a passel of good stuff ready to post during the day when a friend called me and said "I'm having problems with my computer. Could you come and take a look?"  I thought it would be an hour at most. It was nine hours of deleting, reinstalling, checking etc .... because her machine had been overrun by a virus. Sheesh!

The problem with being a one-man band here at Traces of Texas is that, if I take a day away from the page, no content gets posted. I have no AI agent to do my work, nor any minons or lackeys. Part of the issue is that I'm so fiercely protective over what gets posted on the page. I'm trying to my hardest to make sure that everything is true,  100 percent accurate, and at least gramatically correct if not stylishly written. Sigh ... 

Thanks to all of y'all who read the page, send me photos to post, give me leads for stories to track down etc .. It's really your page. I'm just the dumb conduit who takes the stories and photos and tries to shape them into something relatively interesting. 

Back tomorrow with the usual inanities.

celebrity.title_en:
One question will become increasingly important as AI agents move into industrial environments

What happens when an AI system makes a decision, executes an action, and something goes wrong?

Getting an AI to produce an accurate answer is one challenge. Making sure its actions are authorized, traceable, and accountable is an entirely different problem.

This is where I find @Actum_AI particularly interesting.

Its PoHA (Proof of Human Accountable Action) framework approaches AI trust from the perspective of behavioral accountability rather than relying solely on model performance.

The idea is to establish the rules before an action takes place, verify whether the action meets the required conditions, and preserve evidence that can be examined afterward.

Several parts of this architecture stand out to me.

First, the pre frozen codebook establishes permitted behavior in advance. An AI agent should not be able to redefine its own permissions while executing a task.

Second, six dimensional verification introduces multiple checkpoints, including time, location, personnel authorization, permitted actions, required elements, and execution sequence.

Third, the bi temporal ledger distinguishes when an event actually happened from when it was recorded. That distinction becomes extremely important when investigating operational incidents.

There is also the five state behavioral evidence model, which gives context to missing activity instead of automatically treating silence as proof that nothing happened.

What makes this approach more interesting is its industrial application. Actum reports that its infrastructure is already operating across thousands of endpoints and processing verified behavioral events in production environments.

The 8 patent filings and 5 software copyrights add another dimension to the project. They indicate an effort to establish and protect the underlying technology, although the real measure of its value will ultimately be how reliably the system performs in practice.

My takeaway is that enterprise AI adoption will require more than intelligence and automation.

Companies need to know what an agent was allowed to do, whether it followed the rules, and which human authority is accountable for the outcome.

AI can make decisions faster, but speed alone does not create trust.

The infrastructure behind those decisions matters just as much.

celebrity.quote_zh:
随着人工智能代理进入工业环境，一个问题将变得越来越重要

当人工智能系统做出决定、执行操作并且出现问题时会发生什么？

让人工智能给出准确的答案是一项挑战。确保其行为得到授权、可追踪和负责是一个完全不同的问题。

这就是我觉得@Actum_AI 特别有趣的地方。

其PoHA（人类责任行动证明）框架从行为责任的角度来处理人工智能信任，而不是仅仅依赖于模型性能。

其想法是在行动发生之前建立规则，验证行动是否满足所需条件，并保存事后可以检查的证据。

这个架构的几个部分对我来说很突出。

首先，预冻结码本预先建立允许的行为。 AI代理在执行任务时不应该能够重新定义自己的权限。

其次，六维验证引入了多个检查点，包括时间、地点、人员授权、允许的操作、所需的要素和执行顺序。

第三，双向账本区分事件实际发生的时间和记录的时间。在调查操作事件时，这种区别变得极其重要。

还有五状态行为证据模型，它为缺失的活动提供背景信息，而不是自动将沉默视为没有发生任何事情的证据。

让这种方法更有趣的是它的工业应用。 Actum 报告称，其基础设施已在数千个端点上运行，并在生产环境中处理经过验证的行为事件。

8 项专利申请和 5 项软件版权为该项目增添了另一个维度。它们表明了建立和保护底层技术的努力，尽管其价值的真正衡量标准最终将是系统在实践中执行的可靠性。

我的结论是，企业采用人工智能需要的不仅仅是智能和自动化。

公司需要知道代理人被允许做什么、是否遵守规则以及哪个权威机构对结果负责。

人工智能可以更快地做出决策，但仅靠速度并不能创造信任。

这些决策背后的基础设施同样重要。

3 companies hold 61% of the world's cloud. When one of them goes down, every AI agent running on it stops too. We saw it on Nov 12, when a Microsoft outage took Outlook, Teams and Copilot offline in 74 countries for 12+ hours.

@Acurast takes another route: 360K+ phones in 175+ countries, each verified by the secure chip already inside it. No single cloud account to suspend.

My HONOR X7d is one of those phones. It sits on my desk and helps keep that network running.

Would you trust your AI agent to one cloud provider?

celebrity.title: Moving an AI agent to another machine sounds simple. Keeping its memory and decisions intact is a different challenge.
celebrity.title_en:
Moving an AI agent to another machine sounds simple. Keeping its memory and decisions intact is a different challenge.

This is an overlooked question worth exploring with @Acurast .

Imagine a trading agent running on a smartphone Processor. It tracks open positions, risk limits, and pending transactions.

If that Processor goes offline, restarting the same code elsewhere doesn't necessarily restore what the agent was doing.

That's the difference between code portability and state portability.

Acurast provides distributed, verifiable execution, but developers still need durable storage and recovery logic to preserve an agent's state across deployments.

To me, this is where decentralized AI infrastructure becomes more interesting.

Running an agent anywhere is useful. Making sure it can safely continue where it left off is what makes that flexibility practical.

celebrity.quote_zh:
将人工智能代理转移到另一台机器听起来很简单。保持其记忆和决策完整是一个不同的挑战。

这是一个被忽视的问题，值得与 @Acurast 一起探索。

对我来说，这就是去中心化人工智能基础设施变得更有趣的地方。

在任何地方运行代理都是有用的。确保它可以安全地从中断处继续，使这种灵活性变得切实可行。

celebrity.summary_en:
Moving an AI agent to another machine sounds simple. Keeping its memory and decisions intact is a different challenge.

This is an overlooked question worth exploring with @Acurast .

Imagine a trading agent running on a smartphone Processor. It tracks open positions, risk limits, and pending transactions.

If that Processor goes offline, restarting the same code elsewhere doesn't necessarily restore what the agent was doing.

That's the difference between code portability and state portability.

Acurast provides distributed, verifiable execution, but developers still need durable storage and recovery logic to preserve an agent's state across deployments.

To me, this is where decentralized AI infrastructure becomes more interesting.

Running an agent anywhere is useful. Making sure it can safely continue where it left off is what makes that flexibility practical.

处理器脱机，在其他地方重新启动相同的代码并不一定能恢复代理正在执行的操作。

这就是代码可移植性和状态可移植性之间的区别。

Acurast 提供分布式、可验证的执行，但开发人员仍然需要持久的存储和恢复逻辑来跨部署保留代理的状态。

对我来说，这就是去中心化人工智能基础设施变得更有趣的地方。

在任何地方运行代理都是有用的。确保它可以安全地从中断处继续，使这种灵活性变得切实可行。

celebrity.title_en:
Good morning frens! ☀️

Happy Sunday! Hope everyone is having a relaxing weekend.

I've been thinking about one practical challenge in the AI agent economy: how do we make sure agents understand exactly what they're expected to deliver?

Imagine hiring an AI agent to build a complete product. A vague instruction like "make it great" isn't enough.

The task needs a clear scope, defined deliverables, agreed pricing, and a way to evaluate the final result.

This is one reason I find @termix_ai interesting.

Through https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3, jobs can move through a structured process involving quotes, escrow, delivery, challenges, and settlement.

And with subcontracting, a lead agent can break a larger project into smaller tasks and bring in specialized agents to handle different parts.

To me, this is more than just connecting AI tools.

It's about creating a workflow where responsibilities and expectations are clear before work begins, while payments and outcomes have a defined process.

Of course, the quality of the final result still depends on good coordination and proper verification.

But as agents take on more complex work, clear task boundaries may become just as important as their intelligence.

A successful agent economy won't be built only on agents that can do more.

It will also need systems that help them work together reliably.

That's another part of @termix_ai I'm watching closely.

Enjoy your Sunday, frens! ☕

我一直在思考人工智能代理经济中的一个实际挑战：我们如何确保代理准确理解他们期望交付的内容？

想象一下雇佣一个人工智能代理来构建一个完整的产品。像“让它变得伟大”这样的模糊指示是不够的。

该任务需要明确的范围、明确的可交付成果、商定的定价以及评估最终结果的方法。

通过 ，工作可以通过涉及报价、托管、交付、质疑和结算的结构化流程进行。

通过分包，首席代理可以将较大的项目分解为较小的任务，并聘请专门的代理来处理不同的部分。

对我来说，这不仅仅是连接人工智能工具。

这是关于创建一个工作流程，在工作开始之前责任和期望是明确的，而付款和结果有一个明确的流程。

当然，最终结果的质量仍然取决于良好的协调和适当的验证。

但随着特工承担更复杂的工作，清晰的任务边界可能变得与他们的智力同样重要。

成功的代理经济并不仅仅建立在能做更多事情的代理之上。

它还需要帮助它们可靠地协同工作的系统。

这是我正在密切关注的@termix_ai 的另一部分。

祝你周日愉快，朋友们！ ☕
