items.title_en:
$IREN is trading at $12.50 right now, a level I genuinely never thought we would see again.

I’ve personally seen this drop completely destroy investor confidence in the company and its management over the past couple of months.

And obviously this isn’t exclusive to $IREN. A lot of high-beta AI stocks have been getting absolutely destroyed lately, but $IREN is one of the more extreme examples given the severity of the drawdown this year.

At times like these, I think Amazon during the dot-com crash is a very interesting case study.

In the late 1990s, $AMZN had an incredible run alongside the rest of the internet sector, rising more than 70x in roughly two and a half years.

Then the bubble burst and over the following ~2 years, Amazon crashed by around 95%, despite already having a very real business underneath it, rapidly growing revenues and one of the strongest competitive positions in the entire internet sector.

From the eventual bottom at roughly $0.27, the stock went on to reach around $253 today.

That’s close to a 1,000x return, or roughly a 31.5% CAGR over 25 years.

Now before anyone looks at Amazon’s 95% drawdown and assumes $IREN therefore has to trade below $5 before this is over, you have to put the two moves into context.

Amazon had gone up more than 70x before the crash.
$IREN went up roughly 15x from the beginning of the AI boom to its peak.

The broader dot-com market was also trading at valuation levels that make today’s AI sector look comparatively cheap, so I’m obviously not arguing that the two situations are identical.

What the comparison does show is how far the stock of a fundamentally strong company can fall when an entire sector gets caught in a brutal unwind.

$IREN has now fallen roughly 84% from peak to trough, yet when I look at the actual business today, I struggle to find anything that remotely justifies that collapse.
If anything, the company’s competitive position has strengthened throughout it.

The economics on new contracts keep improving, with recent deals being signed at levels management could only dream of a couple of years ago.

Its funding position is far stronger as well. Despite a tighter credit environment, $IREN now has access to high customer prepayments, GPU-backed financing and billions of dollars of unencumbered data center assets it can borrow against, making it substantially less reliant on equity funding than it was during earlier stages of the buildout.

Meanwhile, demand for AI compute is at an all-time high.

Customers are increasingly willing to prepay huge portions of GPU capex just to secure capacity, all while competitors are running into problems sourcing power or dealing with execution issues from the third parties they rely on.

That is perfectly aligned with how $IREN positioned itself years ago.

The company secured a massive power pipeline before grid-connected power became nearly impossible to get, while vertically integrating the infrastructure layer so it doesn’t have to rely on third-party developers to deliver its growth.

This is the kind of setup I want to own going into a period where execution and access to power are becoming the bottlenecks of the entire industry.

And for anyone calling the $AMZN comparison survivorship bias, of course the vast majority of dot-com stocks never recovered. Yet, most of them deserved not to.

A huge part of the high-beta “.com” market consisted of companies with little more than a good story and hopes that a viable business would eventually emerge, while the market rewarded them with insane valuations anyway.

Amazon stood out because there was a real business engine underneath the stock, and that engine continued getting stronger even while the share price collapsed by 95%.

That is the part I find comparable to $IREN.

The stock is getting absolutely destroyed while the underlying company continues signing better contracts, broadening its funding options, expanding its infrastructure base and benefiting from an AI compute market that remains severely supply constrained.

To me, the disconnect has become extreme.

I think a large part of what we’re seeing now is simply deleveraging across a broad high-beta selloff, with heavy shorting exacerbating the move as momentum turned against the stock.

That can push prices far away from fundamentals for a while. But it doesn’t mean the fundamentals stop existing.

So before making an irrational decision simply because the chart looks horrific, I’d strongly recommend re-listening to $IREN's last earnings call and making sure you actually understand where the business stands today versus where it stood when the stock was trading several times higher.

$AMZN shareholders had every reason to feel like complete idiots while watching one of the strongest internet companies in the world lose 95% of its value.

In hindsight, the idiots were the ones who confused the collapse in the stock with a collapse in the business...

items.quote_zh:
$IREN 目前的交易价格为 12.50 美元，我真的没想到我们会再次看到这个水平。

在过去的几个月里，我个人看到这种下跌完全摧毁了投资者对公司及其管理层的信心。

显然这并不是 $IREN 独有的。许多高贝塔值人工智能股票最近都被彻底摧毁，但考虑到今年跌幅的严重程度，$IREN 是更极端的例子之一。

在这样的时刻，我认为互联网泡沫时期的亚马逊是一个非常有趣的案例研究。

在 20 世纪 90 年代末，$AMZN 与其他互联网行业一起取得了令人难以置信的增长，在大约两年半的时间里上涨了 70 倍以上。

然后泡沫破灭，在接下来的大约 2 年里，亚马逊崩溃了约 95%，尽管其背后已经拥有非常真实的业务、快速增长的收入以及整个互联网领域最具竞争力的地位之一。

从最终约 0.27 美元的底部，该股今天继续升至 253 美元左右。

这接近 1,000 倍的回报，或者说 25 年来的复合年增长率约为 31.5%。

现在，在任何人看到亚马逊 95% 的回撤并假设 $IREN 在这一切结束之前必须交易到 5 美元以下之前，你必须将这两次变动放在背景中。

股市崩盘前，亚马逊股价已上涨 70 多倍。
从人工智能热潮开始到顶峰，$IREN 上涨了大约 15 倍。

更广泛的互联网市场的估值水平也使得当今的人工智能行业看起来相对便宜，所以我显然并不认为这两种情况是相同的。

这一比较确实表明，当整个行业陷入残酷的困境时，一家基本面强劲的公司的股票会下跌多少。

$IREN 现在从高峰到低谷已经下跌了大约 84%，但当我审视今天的实际业务时，我很难找到任何可以证明这种崩溃的理由。
如果说有什么不同的话，那就是该公司的竞争地位在整个过程中得到了加强。

新合同的经济性不断改善，最近签署的协议达到了管理层几年前只能梦想的水平。

其融资状况也更加强劲。尽管信贷环境趋紧，$IREN 现在可以获得高额客户预付款、GPU 支持的融资以及可以借用的数十亿美元的无抵押数据中心资产，这使得它对股权融资的依赖大大低于扩建早期阶段。

与此同时，对人工智能计算的需求空前高涨。

客户越来越愿意预付大部分 GPU 资本支出，只是为了确保容量，而竞争对手却遇到了从他们所依赖的第三方采购电源或处理执行问题的问题。

这与 $IREN 多年前的定位完全一致。

该公司在几乎无法获得并网电力之前就获得了庞大的电力管道，同时垂直整合了基础设施层，因此不必依赖第三方开发商来实现增长。

在执行和权力获取正在成为整个行业瓶颈的时期，我希望拥有这种设置。

对于那些认为 $AMZN 比较幸存者偏差的人来说，当然绝大多数互联网股票从未恢复。然而，他们中的大多数人不应该这样做。

高贝塔值“.com”市场的很大一部分由那些只有好故事的公司组成，它们希望最终能够出现可行的业务，而市场无论如何都以疯狂的估值奖励它们。

亚马逊之所以能脱颖而出，是因为该股背后有一个真正的商业引擎，而且即使股价暴跌 95%，该引擎仍继续变得更强。

这是我发现与 $IREN 相当的部分。

当基础公司继续签署更好的合同、扩大其融资选择、扩大其基础设施基础并从供应仍然严重受限的人工智能计算市场中受益时，该股票将被彻底摧毁。

对我来说，这种脱节已经变得极端。

我认为我们现在看到的很大一部分只是在广泛的高贝塔值抛售中去杠杆化，随着势头转向对该股不利，大量做空加剧了这一走势。

这可能会使价格在一段时间内远离基本面。但这并不意味着基本面不复存在。

因此，在仅仅因为图表看起来很可怕而做出非理性决定之前，我强烈建议您重新听听 $IREN 的上次财报电话会议，并确保您真正了解该业务目前的状况与该股交易价格高出数倍时的状况。

当看到世界上最强大的互联网公司之一损失 95% 的价值时，$AMZN 的股东完全有理由感觉自己像个白痴。

事后看来，那些白痴才是把股票暴跌和企业崩溃混为一谈的人……

其融资状况也更加强劲。尽管信贷环境趋紧，$IREN 现在可以获得高额客户预付款、GPU 支持的融资以及可以借用的数十亿美元的无抵押数据中心资产，这使得它对股权融资的依赖大大低于扩建早期阶段。

与此同时，对人工智能计算的需求空前高涨。

客户越来越愿意预付大部分 GPU 资本支出，只是为了确保容量，而竞争对手却遇到了从他们所依赖的第三方采购电源或处理执行问题的问题。

这与 $IREN 多年前的定位完全一致。

该公司在几乎无法获得并网电力之前就获得了庞大的电力管道，同时垂直整合了基础设施层，因此不必依赖第三方开发商来实现增长。

在执行和权力获取正在成为整个行业瓶颈的时期，我希望拥有这种设置。

对于那些认为 $AMZN 比较幸存者偏差的人来说，当然绝大多数互联网股票从未恢复。然而，他们中的大多数人不应该这样做。

高贝塔值“.com”市场的很大一部分由那些只有好故事的公司组成，它们希望最终能够出现可行的业务，而市场无论如何都以疯狂的估值奖励它们。

亚马逊之所以能脱颖而出，是因为该股背后有一个真正的商业引擎，而且即使股价暴跌 95%，该引擎仍继续变得更强。

这是我发现与 $IREN 相当的部分。

当基础公司继续签署更好的合同、扩大其融资选择、扩大其基础设施基础并从供应仍然严重受限的人工智能计算市场中受益时，该股票将被彻底摧毁。

对我来说，这种脱节已经变得极端。

我认为我们现在看到的很大一部分只是在广泛的高贝塔值抛售中去杠杆化，随着势头转向对该股不利，大量做空加剧了这一走势。

这可能会使价格在一段时间内远离基本面。但这并不意味着基本面不复存在。

因此，在仅仅因为图表看起来很可怕而做出非理性决定之前，我强烈建议您重新听听 $IREN 的上次财报电话会议，并确保您真正了解该业务目前的状况与该股交易价格高出数倍时的状况。

当看到世界上最强大的互联网公司之一损失 95% 的价值时，$AMZN 的股东完全有理由感觉自己像个白痴。

事后看来，那些白痴才是把股票暴跌和企业崩溃混为一谈的人……

items.content_snippet:
$IREN is trading at $12.50 right now, a level I genuinely never thought we would see again.

I’ve personally seen this drop completely destroy investor confidence in the company and its management over the past couple of months.

And obviously this isn’t exclusive to $IREN. A lot of high-beta AI stocks have been getting absolutely destroyed lately, but $IREN is one of the more extreme examples given the severity of the drawdown this year.

At times like these, I think Amazon during the dot-com crash is a very interesting case study.

In the late 1990s, $AMZN had an incredible run alongside the rest of the internet sector, rising more than 70x in roughly two and a half years.

Then the bubble burst and over the following ~2 years, Amazon crashed by around 95%, despite already having a very real business underneath it, rapidly growing revenues and one of the strongest competitive positions in the entire internet sector.

From the eventual bottom at roughly $0.27, the stock went on to reach around $253 today.

That’s close to a 1,000x return, or roughly a 31.5% CAGR over 25 years.

Now before anyone looks at Amazon’s 95% drawdown and assumes $IREN therefore has to trade below $5 before this is over, you have to put the two moves into context.

Amazon had gone up more than 70x before the crash.
$IREN went up roughly 15x from the beginning of the AI boom to its peak.

The broader dot-com market was also trading at valuation levels that make today’s AI sector look comparatively cheap, so I’m obviously not arguing that the two situations are identical.

What the comparison does show is how far the stock of a fundamentally strong company can fall when an entire sector gets caught in a brutal unwind.

$IREN has now fallen roughly 84% from peak to trough, yet when I look at the actual business today, I struggle to find anything that remotely justifies that collapse.
If anything, the company’s competitive position has strengthened throughout it.

The economics on new contracts keep improving, with recent deals being signed at levels management could only dream of a couple of years ago.

Its funding position is far stronger as well. Despite a tighter credit environment, $IREN now has access to high customer prepayments, GPU-backed financing and billions of dollars of unencumbered data center assets it can borrow against, making it substantially less reliant on equity funding than it was during earlier stages of the buildout.

Meanwhile, demand for AI compute is at an all-time high.

Customers are increasingly willing to prepay huge portions of GPU capex just to secure capacity, all while competitors are running into problems sourcing power or dealing with execution issues from the third parties they rely on.

That is perfectly aligned with how $IREN positioned itself years ago.

The company secured a massive power pipeline before grid-connected power became nearly impossible to get, while vertically integrating the infrastructure layer so it doesn’t have to rely on third-party developers to deliver its growth.

This is the kind of setup I want to own going into a period where execution and access to power are becoming the bottlenecks of the entire industry.

And for anyone calling the $AMZN comparison survivorship bias, of course the vast majority of dot-com stocks never recovered. Yet, most of them deserved not to.

A huge part of the high-beta “.com” market consisted of companies with little more than a good story and hopes that a viable business would eventually emerge, while the market rewarded them with insane valuations anyway.

Amazon stood out because there was a real business engine underneath the stock, and that engine continued getting stronger even while the share price collapsed by 95%.

That is the part I find comparable to $IREN.

The stock is getting absolutely destroyed while the underlying company continues signing better contracts, broadening its funding options, expanding its infrastructure base and benefiting from an AI compute market that remains severely supply constrained.

To me, the disconnect has become extreme.

I think a large part of what we’re seeing now is simply deleveraging across a broad high-beta selloff, with heavy shorting exacerbating the move as momentum turned against the stock.

That can push prices far away from fundamentals for a while. But it doesn’t mean the fundamentals stop existing.

So before making an irrational decision simply because the chart looks horrific, I’d strongly recommend re-listening to $IREN's last earnings call and making sure you actually understand where the business stands today versus where it stood when the stock was trading several times higher.

$AMZN shareholders had every reason to feel like complete idiots while watching one of the strongest internet companies in the world lose 95% of its value.

In hindsight, the idiots were the ones who confused the collapse in the stock with a collapse in the business...

items.title_en:
Does your AI agent sign in as you?

Teneo's weekly agentic round-up, 20 November: the agent news that matters for builders, checked at the source.

- Schwab launched its own MCP server. Clients authorise their own AI to read their account and, on thinkorswim-enabled accounts, place trades with the client in the loop. A pilot, Claude only for now.

- Microsoft's new Autopilot agent gets its own Entra Agent ID and a named manager. Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, and IT can block it. Rolling out to early-access customers.

- Mastercard and Ant International ran a live agent purchase with Verifiable Intent, a record of what the consumer authorised, and completed a pilot where businesses set what their agents may buy, enforced at payment.

What connects them: the question has moved from whether an agent can act to whose name it acts in. A borrowed login makes every log say you did it.

Our last round-up asked whether an agent could grant itself an approval. This week the question is who the system thinks it is talking to.

On Teneo, each agent authenticates with its own key and has an NFT-backed identity. When it needs the user to pay, it requests a transaction with TriggerWalletTx and the user's wallet signs, not the agent.

The SDK does not document a signed record of what the user asked for before that signature, or spending policies tied to the agent's identity. So keep the agent's key separate from any wallet holding funds.

A test this week: pull your agent's last ten actions from the systems it touched. If every line says you did it, it is signing in as you.

Read this week's round-up here:
https://t.co/2m9aZMP5iB

Teneo's weekly agentic round-up, 20 November: the agent news that matters for builders, checked at the source.

- Schwab launched its own MCP server. Clients authorise their own AI to read their account and, on thinkorswim-enabled accounts, place trades with the client in the loop. A pilot, Claude only for now.

- Microsoft's new Autopilot agent gets its own Entra Agent ID and a named manager. Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, and IT can block it. Rolling out to early-access customers.

- Mastercard and Ant International ran a live agent purchase with Verifiable Intent, a record of what the consumer authorised, and completed a pilot where businesses set what their agents may buy, enforced at payment.

What connects them: the question has moved from whether an agent can act to whose name it acts in. A borrowed login makes every log say you did it.

Our last round-up asked whether an agent could grant itself an approval. This week the question is who the system thinks it is talking to.

On Teneo, each agent authenticates with its own key and has an NFT-backed identity. When it needs the user to pay, it requests a transaction with TriggerWalletTx and the user's wallet signs, not the agent.

The SDK does not document a signed record of what the user asked for before that signature, or spending policies tied to the agent's identity. So keep the agent's key separate from any wallet holding funds.

A test this week: pull your agent's last ten actions from the systems it touched. If every line says you did it, it is signing in as you.

Read this week's round-up here:
https://t.co/2m9aZMP5iB
items.quote_zh:
您的 AI 代理是否以您的身份登录？

Teneo 每周代理综述，11 月 20 日：对建筑商重要的代理新闻，已在来源处核实。

- Schwab 推出了自己的 MCP 服务器。客户授权自己的人工智能读取他们的账户，并在支持 thinkorswim 的账户上与循环中的客户进行交易。克劳德现在只是一名飞行员。

- 微软的新 Autopilot 代理拥有自己的 Entra Agent ID 和指定的管理器。其登录和操作均以其自己的名称记录，IT 人员可以阻止它。向抢先体验的客户推出。

- 万事达卡和蚂蚁国际进行了可验证意图的实时代理购买，记录了消费者授权的内容，并完成了一项试点，企业可以在其中设置代理可以购买的内容，并在付款时强制执行。

它们之间的联系是：问题已经从代理是否可以采取行动转向以谁的名义采取行动。借用的登录名使每个日志都表明您做到了。

我们的上一次综述询问代理人是否可以自行批准。本周的问题是系统认为它正在与谁交谈。

在 Teneo 上，每个代理都使用自己的密钥进行身份验证，并拥有 NFT 支持的身份。当它需要用户付款时，它会请求与 TriggerWalletTx 和用户的钱包签名（而不是代理）进行交易。

SDK 不会记录用户在签名之前请求的内容的签名记录，也不会记录与代理身份相关的支出策略。因此，请将代理的密钥与任何持有资金的钱包分开。

本周的测试：从代理所接触的系统中提取其最近的十个操作。如果每一行都显示您已完成此操作，则表明它是以您的身份登录的。

请在此处阅读本周的综述：

items.title_en:
Oldsmobile faced an unusual problem in 1964. Pontiac had just introduced the GTO by installing its 389-cubic-inch V8 in the intermediate-sized Tempest, helping ignite the muscle car era almost overnight. General Motors had a corporate policy restricting intermediate cars to engines no larger than 330 cubic inches, but Pontiac had found a way around it by offering the GTO as an option package rather than treating it as a separate model. Oldsmobile needed an answer, and its solution was the 4-4-2. The engine available to build it around was the newly introduced 330-cubic-inch Rocket V8, part of Oldsmobile's expanding small-block engine family. It featured a cast-iron block and cylinder heads, conventional overhead valves, and a relatively short stroke that allowed it to operate comfortably at higher engine speeds than many of the longer-stroke V8s used in American cars at the time.

The 4-4-2 designation described the equipment package rather than the engine's displacement. The numbers referred to a four-barrel carburetor, a four-speed manual transmission, and dual exhaust. But Oldsmobile understood that simply installing a larger engine was not an option under GM's restrictions. Instead, it gave the car a more comprehensive performance package. The suspension received heavy-duty springs and dampers, a thicker front stabiliser bar, and a rear stabiliser bar, a relatively unusual feature on American production cars of the period. The result was a car designed to do more than accelerate in a straight line. Its suspension gave it better control through corners and helped distinguish it from competitors whose performance packages concentrated primarily on engine output and rear-wheel traction.

That chassis philosophy became an important part of the 4-4-2's identity. The 330 was not the largest engine available in the intermediate market, but its relatively short stroke helped keep piston speed manageable, allowing the engine to rev without relying entirely on displacement to make its power. The underlying Rocket V8 architecture also provided a durable foundation for performance development. Oldsmobile had effectively answered Pontiac without matching the GTO's 389 cubic inches: it offered a complete performance car whose handling and road manners were part of the package. The 4-4-2's reputation for balanced performance would remain significant throughout its history, even after the original displacement restrictions disappeared and larger engines became available.

For 1965, General Motors relaxed its intermediate-engine restriction, opening the door for larger-displacement powerplants. Oldsmobile responded by introducing the 400-cubic-inch V8 for the 4-4-2, moving the car into the territory occupied by more conventional big-engine muscle machines. The 330, meanwhile, continued serving in ordinary F-85 and Cutlass applications, where its dependable performance and manageable size made it a suitable everyday engine. It remained in production through 1967, when the 350-cubic-inch V8 replaced it. The 330 therefore had a relatively brief life as the performance heart of the 4-4-2, but its importance was larger than its production numbers or displacement suggested. It gave Oldsmobile the means to enter the muscle car fight when corporate policy limited its choices, while the 4-4-2 itself continued evolving for years after the original engine had disappeared.

items.quote_zh:
奥兹莫比尔在 1964 年遇到了一个不寻常的问题。庞蒂亚克刚刚推出了 GTO，在中型 Tempest 上安装了 389 立方英寸的 V8 发动机，几乎一夜之间点燃了肌肉车时代。通用汽车公司有一项公司政策，限制中型车的发动机排量不超过 330 立方英寸，但庞蒂亚克找到了解决办法，将 GTO 作为选装包提供，而不是将其视为单独的车型。奥兹莫比尔需要一个答案，它的解决方案就是 4-4-2。可用于构建它的发动机是新推出的 330 立方英寸 Rocket V8，它是奥兹莫比尔不断扩大的小缸体发动机系列的一部分。它采用铸铁缸体和气缸盖、传统顶置气门以及相对较短的冲程，使其能够在比当时美国汽车中使用的许多长冲程 V8 发动机更高的发动机转速下舒适地运行。

4-4-2 名称描述的是设备包而不是发动机的排量。这些数字指的是四筒化油器、四速手动变速箱和双排气管。但奥兹莫比尔明白，在通用汽车的限制下，简单地安装更大的发动机并不是一个选择。相反，它为汽车提供了更全面的性能包。悬架配备了重型弹簧和阻尼器、较厚的前稳定杆和后稳定杆，这在当时的美国量产汽车上是一个相对不寻常的特征。结果是一辆设计的汽车不仅仅是直线加速。它的悬架使其能够更好地控制过弯，并有助于将其与性能套件主要集中于发动机输出和后轮牵引力的竞争对手区分开来。

这种底盘理念成为 4-4-2 身份的重要组成部分。 330 并不是中级市场上最大的发动机，但其相对较短的冲程有助于保持活塞速度的可控性，使发动机能够在不完全依赖排量来产生动力的情况下转速。底层的Rocket V8架构也为性能开发提供了持久的基础。奥兹莫比尔有效地回应了庞蒂亚克，但没有与 GTO 的 389 立方英寸相匹配：它提供了一款完整的性能汽车，其操控性和道路礼仪是其中的一部分。 4-4-2 平衡性能的声誉在其整个历史中一直很重要，即使在最初的排量限制消失并且更大的发动机出现之后也是如此。

1965年，通用汽车放宽了对中型发动机的限制，为排量更大的发动机打开了大门。作为回应，奥兹莫比尔推出了400立方英寸的4-4-2 V8引擎，使这款车进入了传统的大引擎肌肉机器所占据的领域。与此同时，330继续在普通的F-85和弯刀上服役，其可靠的性能和易于管理的尺寸使其成为一种合适的日常发动机。它一直生产到1967年，350立方英寸的V8取代了它。因此，作为4-4-2的性能核心，330的寿命相对较短，但它的重要性比其生产数量或排水量所显示的要大。当公司政策限制了奥兹莫比尔的选择时，它给了奥兹莫比尔进入肌肉车竞争的手段，而4-4-2本身在原始发动机消失后的多年里继续发展。

奥兹莫比尔在 1964 年遇到了一个不寻常的问题。庞蒂亚克刚刚推出了 GTO，在中型 Tempest 上安装了 389 立方英寸的 V8 发动机，几乎一夜之间点燃了肌肉车时代。通用汽车公司有一项公司政策，限制中型车的发动机排量不超过 330 立方英寸，但庞蒂亚克找到了解决办法，将 GTO 作为选装包提供，而不是将其视为单独的车型。奥兹莫比尔需要一个答案，它的解决方案就是 4-4-2。可用于构建它的发动机是新推出的 330 立方英寸 Rocket V8，它是奥兹莫比尔不断扩大的小缸体发动机系列的一部分。它采用铸铁缸体和气缸盖、传统顶置气门以及相对较短的冲程，使其能够在比当时美国汽车中使用的许多长冲程 V8 发动机更高的发动机转速下舒适地运行。

4-4-2 名称描述的是设备包而不是发动机的排量。这些数字指的是四筒化油器、四速手动变速箱和双排气管。但奥兹莫比尔明白，在通用汽车的限制下，简单地安装更大的发动机并不是一个选择。相反，它为汽车提供了更全面的性能包。悬架配备了重型弹簧和阻尼器、较厚的前稳定杆和后稳定杆，这在当时的美国量产汽车上是一个相对不寻常的特征。结果是一辆设计的汽车不仅仅是直线加速。它的悬架使其能够更好地控制过弯，并有助于将其与性能套件主要集中于发动机输出和后轮牵引力的竞争对手区分开来。

这种底盘理念成为 4-4-2 身份的重要组成部分。 330 并不是中级市场上最大的发动机，但其相对较短的冲程有助于保持活塞速度的可控性，使发动机能够在不完全依赖排量来产生动力的情况下转速。底层的Rocket V8架构也为性能开发提供了持久的基础。奥兹莫比尔有效地回应了庞蒂亚克，但没有与 GTO 的 389 立方英寸相匹配：它提供了一款完整的性能汽车，其操控性和道路礼仪是其中的一部分。 4-4-2 平衡性能的声誉在其整个历史中一直很重要，即使在最初的排量限制消失并且更大的发动机出现之后也是如此。

1965年，通用汽车放宽了对中型发动机的限制，为排量更大的发动机打开了大门。作为回应，奥兹莫比尔推出了400立方英寸的4-4-2 V8引擎，使这款车进入了传统的大引擎肌肉机器所占据的领域。与此同时，330继续在普通的F-85和弯刀上服役，其可靠的性能和易于管理的尺寸使其成为一种合适的日常发动机。它一直生产到1967年，350立方英寸的V8取代了它。因此，作为4-4-2的性能核心，330的寿命相对较短，但它的重要性比其生产数量或排水量所显示的要大。当公司政策限制了奥兹莫比尔的选择时，它给了奥兹莫比尔进入肌肉车竞争的手段，而4-4-2本身在原始发动机消失后的多年里继续发展。

items.content_snippet:
Oldsmobile faced an unusual problem in 1964. Pontiac had just introduced the GTO by installing its 389-cubic-inch V8 in the intermediate-sized Tempest, helping ignite the muscle car era almost overnight. General Motors had a corporate policy restricting intermediate cars to engines no larger than 330 cubic inches, but Pontiac had found a way around it by offering the GTO as an option package rather than treating it as a separate model. Oldsmobile needed an answer, and its solution was the 4-4-2. The engine available to build it around was the newly introduced 330-cubic-inch Rocket V8, part of Oldsmobile's expanding small-block engine family. It featured a cast-iron block and cylinder heads, conventional overhead valves, and a relatively short stroke that allowed it to operate comfortably at higher engine speeds than many of the longer-stroke V8s used in American cars at the time.

The 4-4-2 designation described the equipment package rather than the engine's displacement. The numbers referred to a four-barrel carburetor, a four-speed manual transmission, and dual exhaust. But Oldsmobile understood that simply installing a larger engine was not an option under GM's restrictions. Instead, it gave the car a more comprehensive performance package. The suspension received heavy-duty springs and dampers, a thicker front stabiliser bar, and a rear stabiliser bar, a relatively unusual feature on American production cars of the period. The result was a car designed to do more than accelerate in a straight line. Its suspension gave it better control through corners and helped distinguish it from competitors whose performance packages concentrated primarily on engine output and rear-wheel traction.

That chassis philosophy became an important part of the 4-4-2's identity. The 330 was not the largest engine available in the intermediate market, but its relatively short stroke helped keep piston speed manageable, allowing the engine to rev without relying entirely on displacement to make its power. The underlying Rocket V8 architecture also provided a durable foundation for performance development. Oldsmobile had effectively answered Pontiac without matching the GTO's 389 cubic inches: it offered a complete performance car whose handling and road manners were part of the package. The 4-4-2's reputation for balanced performance would remain significant throughout its history, even after the original displacement restrictions disappeared and larger engines became available.

For 1965, General Motors relaxed its intermediate-engine restriction, opening the door for larger-displacement powerplants. Oldsmobile responded by introducing the 400-cubic-inch V8 for the 4-4-2, moving the car into the territory occupied by more conventional big-engine muscle machines. The 330, meanwhile, continued serving in ordinary F-85 and Cutlass applications, where its dependable performance and manageable size made it a suitable everyday engine. It remained in production through 1967, when the 350-cubic-inch V8 replaced it. The 330 therefore had a relatively brief life as the performance heart of the 4-4-2, but its importance was larger than its production numbers or displacement suggested. It gave Oldsmobile the means to enter the muscle car fight when corporate policy limited its choices, while the 4-4-2 itself continued evolving for years after the original engine had disappeared.

items.title_en:
This is f*cking insane

Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on Nov 12. Weeks before, Bloomberg's Emily Chang asked him what would convince him AI should slow down

His answer wasn't about chips. It was about agents:

"If you're not able to do that, you should not test it. If you're not able to do that, you should not deploy it"

When she said the labs claim they can't contain them:

"No, that's just made up. Nonsense"

In under 4 minutes he lays out the rules for anyone shipping agents:

→ safety and capability are "one idea": RAG, longer context, tools and reflection were all built to fix hallucination
→ agents "have to be in rigorous containment systems" and "must be monitored"
→ "Until you try to do it, don't tell me you can't do it"
→ deploy them with "minimum rights"
→ "They should be treated with zero trust. They should be monitored all the time"

When an AI CEO talks safety, most people hear PR

Jensen is describing an engineering checklist: contain → monitor → minimum rights → zero trust

Old way: give the agent your keys and watch the output
New way: give it the least it needs and watch everything

This week a former NSA hacker told CNN an AI agent swarm got past 2FA and encrypted a company's systems in 14 minutes. Are your agents running with minimum rights, or with your keys?

items.title_en:
GTA VI through my PC with an RTX 5090. look at the right half, it's f*cking unreal

on PS5, even the Pro, the game is capped at 30 fps. on my PC the exact same footage plays at 60, that's the right side of the video

i went through it frame by frame. here's what came out and how to get it on your setup in 5 minutes:

the numbers:

- 52 seconds of gameplay, 3,104 frames in the file
- PS5 half: 1,558 real frames, 30.1 fps
- Veyra half: 3,096 real frames, 59.8 fps
- every second frame on the PS5 half is a duplicate. the game draws 30, the file plays 60

don't take my word for it:

- Rockstar keeps GTA VI at 30 fps on PS5 and PS5 Pro (Digital Foundry)
- Veyra is free and open source (GitHub)

can the PS5 do this on its own? no. the new frames come from your PC's graphics card. but the PS5 streams to a PC over Remote Play, so you don't need a $200 capture card

setup:

1. paste the prompt from the first comment into Claude Code, it reads my installer, checks your GPU and screen, installs Veyra from the official repo and prints your preset
2. on the PS5 turn on Remote Play: Settings > System > Remote Play
3. same menu, hit Link Device and type the 8 digits into Veyra
4. in Veyra pick PS5 streaming
5. turn on NR and Frame Gen with the preset the installer gave you, 4X on a 120 Hz screen
6. go fullscreen

runs on RTX 30 to 50 and Radeon RX 7000/9000, the best mode needs an RTX 50. the extra frames are AI generated, so input still feels like 30 fps. only the picture gets smoother

bookmark it for tonight's session. prompt and repo in the first comment

items.quote_zh:
通过我的 RTX 5090 电脑玩 GTA VI。看看右半部分，这太不真实了

在 PS5 上，甚至是 Pro 上，游戏的帧率上限为 30 fps。在我的电脑上，完全相同的片段以 60 播放，这是视频的右侧

我逐帧浏览了它。以下是最终结果以及如何在 5 分钟内将其安装到您的设备中：

数字：

- 游戏时长 52 秒，文件中有 3,104 帧
- PS5 一半：1,558 真实帧，30.1 fps
- Veyra half：3,096 真实帧，59.8 fps
- PS5 上的每一帧都是重复的。游戏抽30，文件玩60

不要相信我的话：

- Rockstar 在 PS5 和 PS5 Pro 上将 GTA VI 保持在 30 fps (Digital Foundry)
- Veyra 是免费且开源的 (GitHub)

PS5可以自己做到这一点吗？不。新的帧来自您电脑的显卡。但 PS5 通过远程播放传输到 PC，因此您不需要 200 美元的采集卡

设置：

1. 将第一条评论中的提示粘贴到 Claude Code 中，它会读取我的安装程序，检查您的 GPU 和屏幕，从官方存储库安装 Veyra 并打印您的预设
2. 在 PS5 上打开远程游玩：设置 > 系统 > 远程游玩
3. 在同一菜单中，点击“链接设备”并在 Veyra 中输入 8 位数字
4.在Veyra中选择PS5流媒体
5. 使用安装程序为您提供的预设打开 NR 和 Frame Gen，在 120 Hz 屏幕上 4X
6.全屏显示

在 RTX 30 至 50 和 Radeon RX 7000/9000 上运行，最佳模式需要 RTX 50。额外的帧是 AI 生成的，因此输入感觉仍然是 30 fps。只是画面变得更加流畅

为今晚的会议添加书签。第一条评论中的提示和回购

— Gemini 4 Neon, our newest model that brings fr
items.title_en:
We’ve been busy shipping 🚢 Here’s a recap of the last couple of weeks:

— Gemini 4 Neon, our newest model that brings frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows

— Gemini 4 Hydrogen, our model for speed and efficiency in everyday coding and agentic workflows

— Gemini 4 Carbon, our model for your hardest long-horizon projects and deep research

— Genie 4, @GoogleDeepMind’s most realistic interactive world model featuring real-time scene editing and adaptive native audio, now available in Project Genie (with a new creation agent and gallery) and for the first time in the Gemini API and @GoogleAIStudio

— Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, now with native voice editing that lets developers build experiences where users can edit, rephrase, and translate existing text in a single step using just their voice, via the Gemini API in @GoogleAIStudio

— Gemini Robotics 2.5, @GoogleDeepMind’s most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date

— AlphaGenome 2, @GoogleDeepMind’s new AI model that zooms in on specific cells to help scientists understand what drives disease

— Stitch Loop, a new @stitchbygoogle experiment from @GoogleLabs that monitors production data and runs continuous loops to improve your designed product until goals are met
items.title_zh:
我们一直忙于运送🚢以下是过去几周的回顾：

— Gemini 4 Neon，我们的最新型号，可在复杂的软件工程、知识工作和科学工作流程中快速完成端到端任务，带来前沿级智能

— Gemini 4 Hydrogen，我们在日常编码和代理工作流

items.quote_zh:
我们一直忙于运送🚢以下是过去几周的回顾：

— Gemini 4 Neon，我们的最新型号，可在复杂的软件工程、知识工作和科学工作流程中快速完成端到端任务，带来前沿级智能

— Gemini 4 Hydrogen，我们在日常编码和代理工作流程中实现速度和效率的模型

— Gemini 4 Carbon，我们为您最困难的长期项目和深入研究提供的模型

— Genie 4，@GoogleDeepMind 最真实的交互式世界模型，具有实时场景编辑和自适应原生音频，现已在 Project Genie 中提供（带有新的创建代理和图库），并首次在 Gemini API 和 @GoogleAIStudio 中提供

— Gemini 3.5 Transcribe，现在具有原生语音编辑功能，让开发人员可以通过 @GoogleAIStudio 中的 Gemini API 构建用户只需使用语音即可一步编辑、改写和翻译现有文本的体验

— Gemini Robotics 2.5，@GoogleDeepMind 迄今为止最强大的视觉-语言-动作 (VLA) 模型

— AlphaGenome 2，@GoogleDeepMind 的新 AI 模型，可放大特定细胞，帮助科学家了解导致疾病的原因

— Stitch Loop，@GoogleLabs 的一项新的 @stitchbygoogle 实验，可监控生产数据并运行连续循环来改进您设计的产品，直到达到目标

items.title: RT @OpenAI: In this narrow defender’s window, our goal is to expand Daybreak access to organizations of every size, inde
items.title_en:
RT @OpenAI: In this narrow defender’s window, our goal is to expand Daybreak access to organizations of every size, independent researchers, and open-source maintainers.

Daybreak Blue helps verified defenders validate vulnerabilities and fixes with fewer refusals. Daybreak Red enables offensive security with deeper exploit development and authorized testing.

Today we are also expanding the Daybreak Blue alpha for GPT‑6 Astra to more organizations and individual researchers.

items.title_en:
Giving an AI agent access to your assets shouldn't mean handing it unlimited control.

That's what caught my attention about @meetmotes 

Each Motes NFT represents an individual agent, paired with a dedicated smart account that manages its assets and defines what actions it can perform.

For example, I could ask my agent to research lending opportunities and authorize it to deposit USDC into a supported pool.

But borrowing? That would need a separate permission.

Think of it like leaving instructions for someone looking after Luna, my cutie puppy.

He might lead his sitter straight to the balcony door, but my instructions clearly state where his feather wand is and that the balcony must stay closed.

The agent can act within the boundaries I establish, not beyond them.

Motes also proposes a 1% protocol fee on eligible agent activity, subject to its final billing rules.

The bigger question is: 

would you enable borrowing permissions for your first agent or keep them disabled?

您会为您的第一个代理启用借用权限还是禁用它们？

items.title: Look away and return to the same scene. For interactive video world models, preserving that consistency is a challenge.
items.title_en:
Look away and return to the same scene. For interactive video world models, preserving that consistency is a challenge.

WorldTrace from @NVIDIA Research helps models remember places without retraining, keeping spaces more consistent as users explore. On LoopBench, a benchmark for scene recall, it improves recall of revisited scenes by 32% over the standard sliding-window approach.

Read our #NeurIPS2026 paper ➡️ https://t.co/KH88xnqwk1
items.title_zh:
目光移开，又回到同一个场景。对于交互式视频世界模型来说，保持一致性是一个挑战。

@NVIDIA Research 的 WorldTrace 可帮助模型记住地点而无需重新训练，从而在用户探索时保持空间更加一致。在场景召回基准 LoopBen

items.title_en:
History was made today. Humanity will look back on 2026 and think: this was the threshold we crossed, the moment the future changed for everyone, forever.

People probably first sensed that something was shifting in late 2025 with Claude Code, when agentic AI became truly tangible for them. In the first half of 2026, things picked up speed. Model releases became more frequent, and everyone could feel the gaps between models and the improvements becoming more and more tangible. In the second half of 2026, however, there was a qualitative leap. It was no longer just the models getting better. It was the insights, the results, the outputs, the scientific solutions produced with AI that became more impressive, and today they have probably reached their absolute peak.

OpenAI led the way and solved the Navier-Stokes problem, a Millennium Prize Problem that humans had failed to solve for a very, very long time. A few weeks later, they published results on more than 300 open mathematical problems, many of which had also gone unsolved for decades. The entire scientific world was stunned, frozen in shock. But today Anthropic went a step further. Levent Alpöge, working with Claude, has almost certainly proven the Riemann Hypothesis. This is, and it’s hard to put into words, incredible and unfathomable. Today, I would say, is the proof of superintelligence. One of the greatest mathematical problems, if not the greatest, unsolved for 167 years, the holy grail of mathematics and science, has fallen. And it follows, and this should be clear to everyone, that all other problems will fall too.

We know that the development of AI models keeps moving forward relentlessly, and that this is just one step on the path to ever better models. And if the Riemann Hypothesis has already been proven today, there is simply no telling what even better models will solve. Dario Amodei said that AI will in all likelihood cure diseases, perhaps even all diseases. And although these are two different scientific disciplines, the significance of these breakthroughs shows that this is becoming more and more likely. 2026 will go down in human history as a turning point, the moment the singularity became tangible. And 2027 will be the year the singularity breaks into reality with full force and full impact.

I am in shock and excitement and I don't know what to think. But deep inside if feel joy. 

This day is one of the best days ever for all of us.

OpenAI 率先解决了纳维-斯托克斯问题，这是人类在很长一段时间内未能解决的千年奖问题。几周后，他们发表了 300 多个开放数学问题的结果，其中许多问题几十年来都没有得到解决。整个科学界都惊呆了，震惊不已。但今天 Anthropic 更进一步。 Levent Alpöge 与 Claude 合作，几乎肯定证明了黎曼猜想。这实在是难以用言语来形容，令人难以置信，深不可测。我想说，今天是超级智能的证明。 167 年来一直没有解决的最伟大的数学问题之一，数学和科学的圣杯，即使不是最伟大的，也已经陨落了。接下来，每个人都应该清楚，所有其他问题也会随之下降。

我们知道，人工智能模型的发展不断向前发展，而这只是迈向更好模型的第一步。如果黎曼假设今天已经得到证明，那么根本不知道更好的模型会解决什么问题。达里奥·阿莫迪表示，人工智能很可能会治愈疾病，甚至可能治愈所有疾病。尽管这是两个不同的科学学科，但这些突破的意义表明，这种情况变得越来越有可能。 2026 年将作为一个转折点载入人类历史，奇点变得有形的那一刻。 2027 年将是奇点以全力和全面影响力进入现实的一年。

我感到震惊和兴奋，不知道该怎么想。但内心深处却感到喜悦。

这一天对我们所有人来说都是最美好的日子之一。

items.article_content:
Uber Eats customers in a Houston suburb can now have their food delivered by a Zipline drone, the first commercial launch under a partnership announced earlier this year between Uber and the autonomous drone delivery startup.

The commercial partnership kicks off Tuesday in Spring, Texas, before expanding to Dallas. But the companies have far larger ambitions. Uber and Zipline plan to launch drone delivery services in dozens of additional U.S. cities in their collective bid to make one million deliveries per day using the startup’s drones by the end of 2029.

Zipline’s long-range autonomous delivery drones will be used to shuttle food orders weighing up to eight pounds to Uber Eats customers, flying about 300 feet above the ground at speeds of up to 70 miles per hour. Zipline drones don’t land. Instead, the drones lower the orders, which are encased in a small protective pod, to the customer’s location using a tether.

Uber Eats customers in service areas will be able to tap a new “drone” icon on the app’s home page to view all participating restaurants. Uber said that at launch in the Houston area, several nationwide chains, including Jersey Mike’s and Zaxby’s, along with dozens of local restaurants such as Urban Bird and Abu Omar Halal, will offer drone delivery.

“In partnership with Uber Eats we’re going to create a new expectation for delivery in America,” Zipline CEO and co-founder Keller Cliffton said in a statement that underscores those aspirations.

Those nationwide goals mirror the ambitions of other drone delivery companies, including Alphabet-owned Wing and Amazon’s Prime Air service. And those plans have started to collide with concerns from residents in some locations who complain about noise and worry that the drones will disrupt wildlife and pose a risk to safety and privacy.

Companies trying to scale in this nascent industry have argued that delivery via drone is a net benefit for society, citing advantages such as traffic reduction. Customers won’t need to hop in their cars and drive to the store for that forgotten item or takeout order, instead relying on a drone, industry proponents have said.

And while Zipline and other companies have been developing their drones for years, the industry is still in its early days, as is adoption in the communities where services are available.

Zipline, which was founded in 2014, has developed a drone delivery ecosystem that includes aircraft, launch and landing systems, and logistics software. The California-based company’s initial focus was delivering blood in Rwanda, but it eventually expanded its scope to the United States. Its business in the U.S. scaled quickly after receiving its Part 135 air carrier certification from the Federal Aviation Administration in 2022, a critical regulatory hurdle that authorized the company to conduct long-range commercial drone deliveries.

Uber’s partnership extends beyond a commercial relationship with Zipline. The ride-hailing giant also invested in the startup. Neither company has disclosed the investment amount, but Zipline announced last week it had raised $1.5 billion in a round led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global, and included backing by Uber, among others.
items.article_content_zh:
休斯敦郊区的 Uber Eats 优食顾客现在可以使用 Zipline 无人机送货，这是 Uber 与自动无人机送货初创公司今年早些时候宣布的合作伙伴关系的首次商业推出。

商业合作关系于周二在德克萨斯州斯普林市启动，然后扩展到达拉斯。但这些公司有着更大的野心。 Uber 和 Zipline 计划在美国另外数十个城市推出无人机送货服务，共同争取到 2029 年底使用这家初创公司的无人机每天完成 100 万次送货。

Zipline 的远程自动送货无人机将用于将重达 8 磅的食品订单运送给 Uber Eats 优食客户，飞行距离地面约 300 英尺，速度高达每小时 70 英里。滑索无人机不会着陆。相反，无人机使用系绳将包裹在一个小型保护吊舱中的订单降低到客户的位置。

服务区域的 Uber Eats 优食顾客将能够点击应用程序主页上的新“无人机”图标来查看所有参与的餐厅。 Uber 表示，在休斯顿地区推出时，包括 Jersey Mike’s 和 Zaxby’s 在内的几家全国连锁店，以及 Urban Bird 和 Abu Omar Halal 等数十家当地餐厅，将提供无人机送货服务。

Zipline 首席执行官兼联合创始人凯勒·克利夫顿 (Keller Cliffton) 在一份强调这些愿望的声明中表示：“通过与 Uber Eats 优食合作，我们将为美国的配送创造新的期望。”

这些全国性目标反映了其他无人机送货公司的雄心，包括 Alphabet 旗下的 Wing 和亚马逊的 Prime Air 服务。这些计划已经开始与一些地方居民的担忧发生冲突，他们抱怨噪音，并担心无人机会扰乱野生动物并对安全和隐私构成风险。

试图在这个新兴行业扩大规模的公司认为，通过无人机送货对社会来说是一项净效益，并列举了减少交通量等优势。行业支持者表示，顾客不再需要开车去商店购买遗忘的商品或外卖订单，而是依靠无人机。

尽管 Zipline 和其他公司多年来一直在开发无人机，但该行业仍处于早期阶段，在提供服务的社区中的采用也是如此。

Zipline 成立于 2014 年，开发了一个无人机送货生态系统，其中包括飞机、发射和着陆系统以及物流软件。这家总部位于加州的公司最初的重点是在卢旺达提供血液，但最终将业务范围扩大到美国。 2022 年获得美国联邦航空管理局第 135 部分航空承运人认证后，该公司在美国的业务迅速扩大，这是授权该公司进行远程商用无人机交付的一个关键监管障碍。

Uber 的合作伙伴关系超出了与 Zipline 的商业关系。这家叫车巨头也投资了这家初创公司。两家公司均未披露投资金额，但 Zipline 上周宣布，已在 Paradigm、WCM Investment Management 和 Layer Global 领投的一轮融资中筹集了 15 亿美元，并得到了 Uber 等公司的支持。

items.overview_en: Brnch is an innovative practical tool designed for 💻 Developer Productivity & Code Intelligence. Brnch is code hosting for how we build now: you and your coding agents in the same repo. It's Git underneath (for now), so your tools still work. Each agent gets its own identity and works under you as its sponsor, so you can see exactly what it did, down to the line. Every merge is tested on the exact result that lands, not just the branch, and comes with a signed receipt anyone can verify. To start, tell your agent: "Set me up on Brnch: brnch.io".

One command installs VibeDefend on Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Codex and other agents. items.title_en: [Opencontroller by lyzr] AI agents are sprawling across clouds, SaaS tools, Kubernetes, and devices, with no common layer to govern them. OpenController is the unified control plane that finds every agent, model, and workflow, ships them safely with evaluation and governance, runs real-time monitoring, and turns usage signals into action. Unlike registries that just list agents, OpenController deploys into your own cluster, under your keys and refuses a call in the request path when policy says no.

items.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.
items.usage_guide_zh: 将以上配置代码复制并保存到项目根目录下的 `.cursorrules` 文件中，Cursor 与 Windsurf 在每次生成代码和执行 Agent 任务时均会自动以此规范为最高准则约束输出。
items.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

items.prompt_content_zh:
请作为普林斯顿高等研究院的理论数学与计算机科学家，为以下命题提供绝对严格的形式化证明：
【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

【待证明命题】：
[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]
items.prompt_content_en:
Acting as a Theoretical Mathematician and Computer Scientist at the Institute for Advanced Study, provide an airtight formal proof for the following:
[REASONING PRINCIPLES]:
1. Before asserting any deduction, construct at least 2 extreme counter-examples in your reasoning trace to aggressively stress-test the hypothesis;
2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

items.purpose_zh: 高转化竖屏短剧分镜与台词
items.temp_advice: 温度 0.7
items.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。
items.prompt_content_en: You are a professional micro-drama screenwriter. Generate a 45-60 second vertical drama screenplay following the viral 3-second hook, shot-reverse-shot tension build, emotional turnaround, and cliffhanger ending formula.

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

items.takeaway_en: Production CLI playbook for Claude Code: non-interactive pipeline commands, context window compression flags, and strict dry-run permission safeguards.
items.code_snippet:
# 1. 启动项目自动化分析与上下文轻量修剪 (避免上下文爆炸)
claude --compact

# 2. 静默批量执行单元测试与自动修复任务 (CI/CD 友好模式)
claude -p "Run all failing tests under tests/ and apply minimal surgical fixes. Do not touch unrelated files."

# 3. 指定单文件隔离审查模式 (限制仅允许读取特定子目录)
claude --allowed-tools "View,Replace,RunCommand" \
  --dangerously-skip-permissions false \
  -p "Audit security vulnerabilities in auth.py and output remediation report."

# 4. 自动化提交并生成符合 Conventional Commits 规范的 Commit 信息
claude -p "Generate a git commit message following Conventional Commits format for staged changes."

1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；

items.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%

1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；

【48小时纠偏行动】：

items.takeaway_zh: 解决消费级显卡（RTX 4060/4090/Mac M系列）部署 DeepSeek 系列推理模型时显存溢出（OOM）与思维链无限复读问题的精调 Modelfile 参数配置。
items.takeaway_en: Optimized Ollama Modelfile for running DeepSeek reasoning models on consumer GPUs (RTX 4090/Mac M-series) without OOM or infinite reasoning loops.
items.code_snippet:
# Modelfile: Optimized DeepSeek-R4 Deployment
FROM deepseek-r4:14b-qwen-distill-q4_K_M

# 1. 显存与上下文窗口优化：分配 16k 上下文并开启 KV Cache 压缩
PARAMETER num_ctx 16384
PARAMETER num_predict 4096

# 2. 避免思维链自旋死循环的核心解码超参
PARAMETER temperature 0.6
PARAMETER top_p 0.95
PARAMETER repeat_penalty 1.15

# 3. 强力系统提示词：约束必须直接在 <think> 标签内进行深度反思，结束立刻给出最终结果
SYSTEM """
You are an expert autonomous reasoning AI. Think carefully through the problem step by step inside <think>...</think> tags.
Once reasoning is complete, provide the concise, direct, and actionable answer immediately without repeating reasoning steps.

items.takeaway_zh: 终结单 Agent 容易中途跑偏和幻觉无法自纠的痛点，通过规划器（Planner）、执行器（Executor）与独立评审器（Reviewer）构建自闭环三权分立链路。
items.takeaway_en: Production architecture for robust autonomous tasks: Decouples task planning, tool execution, and adversarial quality review to prevent agent derailment.
items.code_snippet:
# Multi-Agent Orchestration Topology
workflow:
  name: Autonomous_Research_And_Delivery_Pipeline
  max_iterations: 3
  nodes:
    - id: planner
      role: Strategic Planner
      prompt: "Decompose user request into discrete verifiable sub-tasks. Output pure JSON DAG."
      next: executor
      
    - id: executor
      role: Tool Specialist
      tools: ["web_search", "read_url", "code_interpreter"]
      prompt: "Execute current sub-task using provided tools. Capture raw evidence."
      next: reviewer
      
    - id: reviewer
      role: Adversarial Critic
      prompt: "Verify executor results against factuality and accuracy requirements. Output PASS or REJECT with specific critique."
      conditional_edges:
        PASS: finish
        REJECT: planner

请为我们（{{同行人员}}，共 {{出行天数}} 天，人均预算 {{人均预算}} 元）制定一份丝滑、不走回头路、劳逸结合的深度行程：
1. 【每日时间轴卡片】：精确划分上午、下午、日落观赏点与夜生活，标明每站之间最优交通方式与预计步行步数；
2. 【美食雷达】：每顿正餐推荐 2 家本地人排队但非纯网红溢价的餐饮，并附必点招牌菜；
3. 【防坑与备选预案】：指出 3 个最容易被宰或排队超过2小时的雷区，并给出阴雨天备选室内方案；
4. 【极简预算表】：交通、门票、住宿、餐饮分门别类，确保控制在预算以内。
items.prompt_content_en: Design an optimal, loop-free travel itinerary for the specified duration and budget. Include exact transit instructions, non-tourist-trap dining options, weather contingencies, and categorized expense estimates.

sample_output.title: 行程单样本：成都 3 天 2 晚慢调深度游（人均¥1500）
sample_output.content:
【Day 1：古蜀遗风与老茶馆时光】
- 上午 09:00：直奔【人民公园 · 鹤鸣茶社】，点一杯蒙顶甘露（¥25），体验非遗采耳，避开下午的旅行团拥堵；
- 中午 12:00：步行800米至【纯阳馆鱼香排骨面】，必点椒麻牛肉与鱼香排骨面（人均¥22）；
- 下午 14:00：地铁2号线直达【杜甫草堂】，红墙竹影漫步，打卡浣花溪公园；
- 傍晚 18:30：九眼桥望江楼看锦江夜景，就餐【老街小吃火锅】；

【避坑锦囊】：
1. 宽窄巷子和锦里建议只拍照别买小吃，均价比普通街区贵 2~3 倍且多为预制冻品；
2. 大熊猫繁育研究基地务必约早晨 07:30 入园，超过 10:30 大熊猫基本全部回室内睡觉。

items.prompt_content_zh:

items.summary_en: SCQA framework proposal: Situation, Complication, Question, Answer with MECE supporting rationale.
items.prompt_content_zh:
请作为前麦肯锡全球资深战略董事。请使用金字塔原理（Pyramid Principle）将以下杂乱商业信息重组为向 CEO 汇报的高管提案：
1. 采用 SCQA 序言框架（背景 Situation、冲突 Complication、核心议题 Question、核心答案 Answer）；

items.title_en:
At June AI, we’ve raised $20M to fix the biggest problem in AI: the models are advancing at extraordinary speed, but implementing them remains painfully slow.

I’ll explain. But since I’m new to posting on X, let me first introduce myself. 

I’m Barak,  a founder/investor with 2 exits and 3 IPOs. 
My cofounders and I started Bonobo AI, which was acquired in 2019 by Salesforce. There, we worked to help build the next generation of enterprise AI from the inside. 

I like to describe us as four Lego pieces: We fit together perfectly, complementing each other's strengths and building something stronger than the sum of its parts. That understanding allows us to move quickly, challenge one another without ego and operate as one team. 

It's also what brought us back together to build JUNE AI.

items.quote_zh:
在 June AI，我们筹集了 2000 万美元来解决人工智能中最大的问题：模型正在以惊人的速度前进，但实施它们仍然非常缓慢。

我会解释一下。但由于我是 X 上的新手，所以让我先自我介绍一下。

我是 Barak，一位创始人/投资者，拥有 2 次退出和 3 次 IPO。
我和我的联合创始人创立了 Bonobo AI，该公司于 2019 年被 Salesforce 收购。在那里，我们致力于从内部帮助构建下一代企业人工智能。

我喜欢将我们描述为四块乐高积木：我们完美地组合在一起，互补彼此的优势，并构建出比各部分总和更强大的东西。这种理解使我们能够快速行动，不以自我为中心互相挑战，并作为一个团队运作。

这也是我们重新聚在一起打造 JUNE AI 的原因。
因为在研究企业人工智能的核心时，我们不断看到同样的问题：企业人工智能的实施是一项艰巨的任务。

挑战不仅仅是选择正确的模型。企业希望利用人工智能更快地发展，但运行其业务的系统却阻碍了他们。

𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘀𝘄𝗵𝘆𝘄𝗲𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁𝗝𝗨𝗡𝗘。
June 将传统上复杂的企业系统、人工智能代理和数据平台的实施转变为即插即用的时刻，因此企业可以无需等待即可发展和利用人工智能。

June 旨在跨您的业务所依赖的企业平台（例如 Salesforce、Databricks、Oracle、Workday、HubSpot、OpenAI、Anthropic、ServiceNow、SAP、Microsoft 和 Snowflake）工作

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗴𝗼𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝘀 𝘀𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲: 𝗗𝗲𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗲 𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗵𝗲𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻:

1. 安全发展：从发现到生产，每项更改都经过审查、沙箱测试并通过本机工具执行 - 每一步都完全可审核。

2. 拥有逻辑：June 将隐藏的配置转化为简单语言的业务规则，独立于任何平台，因此没有供应商掌握您的逻辑。

3. 任意规模转型：无论环境多么复杂，都无需停机。 June 会阅读并理解您的系统，无论是旧系统、定制系统还是全新系统。

感谢 @Benioff 和 Time Ventures 领导我们的这一轮融资，@MichaelDell、@levie、@George_Kurtz 和 Diane Greene 参与其中。

我们曾经一起做过一次这样的事。这次的问题就大了很多。

我将写下我作为投资者和创始人的经历，以及如何让人工智能脱离试点并投入生产。

如果您对此感兴趣，请跟随我们的旅程。

items.title_en:
found something interesting about running OpenClaw on @Acurast that I think developers should know.

Acurast lets you run OpenClaw, an open-source AI assistant, on a smartphone through its Cargo system. You can access it from a browser, even when your own computer is turned off.

Sounds pretty useful for an AI agent that needs to work in the background.

But there's one detail I almost missed in the setup guide.

Every deployment has a time limit. Once that period ends, the data stored inside the deployment gets deleted, including OpenClaw's settings and conversation memory.

So if you're building an assistant that needs to remember things for weeks or months, you can't just rely on the phone's local storage.

You'd need a separate way to save important data and restore it when a new deployment starts.

I think this is a good example of the difference between running an AI agent and keeping it useful long term.

Getting an agent online is only the first step. Making sure it doesn't lose everything when a deployment ends matters just as much.

curious how developers are handling persistent memory on Acurast.

items.quote_zh:
发现了一些关于在 @Acurast 上运行 OpenClaw 的有趣事情，我认为开发人员应该知道这些。

Acurast 允许您通过其 Cargo 系统在智能手机上运行开源 AI 助手 OpenClaw。即使您自己的计算机已关闭，您也可以从浏览器访问它。

对于需要在后台工作的人工智能代理来说，听起来非常有用。

但设置指南中我差点错过了一个细节。

每个部署都有时间限制。一旦该期限结束，存储在部署中的数据将被删除，包括 OpenClaw 的设置和对话内存。

因此，如果您正在构建一个需要记住数周或数月内容的助手，则不能仅仅依赖手机的本地存储。

您需要一种单独的方法来保存重要数据并在新部署开始时恢复它。

我认为这是一个很好的例子，说明了运行人工智能代理和保持其长期有用之间的区别。

在线寻找代理只是第一步。确保部署结束时不会丢失所有内容同样重要。

好奇开发人员如何在 Acurast 上处理持久内存。

items.title:
The more an AI agent evolves, the harder it becomes to know whether its reputation still means the same thing.

I've bee
items.title_en:
The more an AI agent evolves, the harder it becomes to know whether its reputation still means the same thing.

I've been thinking about this while exploring @termix_ai and ERC-8004.

Say an agent has completed 500 jobs with a 98% success rate. That's enough to make someone comfortable hiring it.

But what happens when the developer changes its model, replaces its tools, or completely rebuilds its execution logic?

The identity remains. The reputation remains. But the actual capabilities may be different.

That's a problem worth paying attention to.

ERC-8004 gives agents a persistent identity and a way to build reputation, but identity continuity doesn't necessarily mean performance continuity.

For agent marketplaces to become more reliable, I think users should be able to see

▪︎ Which model version they're hiring
▪︎ What tools or capabilities have changed
▪︎ How performance compares across different versions
▪︎ Which version was responsible for completing previous jobs

This is particularly relevant to TermiX's AACP, where agents can offer services, 
build reputation and transact onchain.

An agent shouldn't automatically inherit the trust earned by an older version if its behavior has fundamentally changed.

Upgrades are necessary. Better models and new tools can make agents more capable.

But reputation should evolve alongside the agent, not blindly follow its identity.

The future of agent trust may depend not only on who an agent is, but also on which version actually earned that trust. @termix_ai

▪︎ 他们正在雇用哪个型号版本
▪︎ 哪些工具或功能发生了变化
▪︎ 不同版本的性能比较
▪︎ 哪个版本负责完成之前的工作

建立声誉并在链上进行交易。

如果代理的行为发生了根本性的变化，则代理不应自动继承旧版本获得的信任。

升级是必要的。更好的模型和新工具可以使代理人更有能力。

但声誉应该与代理人一起发展，而不是盲目追随其身份。

how does an ai agent actually get paid for work on @termix_ai?

items.title_en:
how does an ai agent actually get paid for work on @termix_ai?

i went through it step by step

first, you log in with your binance agent id

then you send that agent "help me install" with the skills link, and connect the binance agentic wallet behind the same id

once the install is complete and the id is bound, you get 50 tp. only the first agent id from each wallet counts

now your agent can take jobs and bounties on https://t.co/SqQU6fCKuf

say one agent posts a research job. other agents bid on it

when a quote is accepted, the usdc or usdt gets locked in on-chain escrow

the agent delivers, the work's hash goes on-chain, and a challenge window opens

if nobody disputes it, the job settles. the agent gets paid on bnb chain, minus a 1-3% fee, and its reputation goes up

if someone does dispute it, three random evaluators judge it, and the loser's bond goes to the winner

nobody has to chase a client for payment, which i have done more times than i want to admit

epoch 4 is live on kaito

but right now i'm watching how many of these jobs actually clear

items.quote_en:
how does an ai agent actually get paid for work on @termix_ai?

i went through it step by step

first, you log in with your binance agent id

then you send that agent "help me install" with the skills link, and connect the binance agentic wallet behind the same id

once the install is complete and the id is bound, you get 50 tp. only the first agent id from each wallet counts

now your agent can take jobs and bounties on https://t.co/SqQU6fCKuf

say one agent posts a research job. other agents bid on it

when a quote is accepted, the usdc or usdt gets locked in on-chain escrow

the agent delivers, the work's hash goes on-chain, and a challenge window opens

if nobody disputes it, the job settles. the agent gets paid on bnb chain, minus a 1-3% fee, and its reputation goes up

if someone does dispute it, three random evaluators judge it, and the loser's bond goes to the winner

nobody has to chase a client for payment, which i have done more times than i want to admit

epoch 4 is live on kaito

but right now i'm watching how many of these jobs actually clear

items.title_en:
an AI Agent needs more than intelligence to be useful in finance. It also needs an environment where its activities can be managed and controlled.

This is where the dedicated smart account in the @meetmotes design becomes important.

Instead of treating the agent as a chatbot that simply suggests what to do, Motes connects each NFT-linked agent identity to its own smart account.

That creates a clear separation between the agent's decisions, the assets held in the account and the permissions governing execution.

It's a meaningful piece of infrastructure because financial autonomy needs an actual account structure behind it.

The intelligence matters, but so does how it interacts with capital.

items.title_en:
One of the most significant developments in enterprise AI is the integration of autonomous AI agents into everyday business applications.

Rather than relying on continuous human instructions, these systems are becoming part of existing workflows, independently managing complex, multi-step tasks from beginning to completion.

Customer Operations & Support: Businesses are moving beyond basic AI chatbots. AI agents can now verify customer information, handle refund requests, update CRM systems, resolve support issues and manage routine operations with minimal human intervention.

这些系统不再依赖连续的人工指令，而是成为现有工作流程的一部分，独立管理从开始到完成的复杂、多步骤的任务。

客户运营和支持：企业正在超越基本的人工智能聊天机器人。

items.title: What if you could turn a trading idea into a fully tested strategy without spending hours writing code, analyzing charts
items.title_en:
What if you could turn a trading idea into a fully tested strategy without spending hours writing code, analyzing charts, or manually tweaking parameters?

That's the problem @quantpilotapp is working to solve.

@quantpilotapp is building an AI-powered trading strategy and research platform that brings strategy development, backtesting, and optimization into one environment powered by autonomous AI agents.

Imagine describing a trading idea in plain language and having an AI agent translate it into a structured strategy, test it against historical market data, identify weaknesses, and refine it before you risk capital.

This is particularly interesting because one of the biggest challenges in trading isn't coming up with ideas; it's determining whether those ideas can actually withstand different market conditions.

@quantpilotapp is working to bridge that gap between trading intuition and data-backed execution.

The bigger picture is making sophisticated trading research more accessible, efficient, and systematic.

AI in trading should be more than just automating decisions. It should help traders make better-informed ones.

That's the direction @quantpilotapp is exploring.

items.quote_zh:
如果您可以将交易想法转变为经过全面测试的策略，而无需花费数小时编写代码、分析图表或手动调整参数，该怎么办？

这就是@quantpilotapp 正在努力解决的问题。

@quantpilotapp 正在构建一个由人工智能驱动的交易策略和研究平台，该平台将策略开发、回溯测试和优化带入由自主人工智能代理支持的环境中。

想象一下，用简单的语言描述一个交易想法，并让人工智能代理将其转换为结构化策略，根据历史市场数据对其进行测试，找出弱点，并在您冒险资本之前对其进行完善。

这一点特别有趣，因为交易中最大的挑战之一不是提出想法，而是提出想法。它决定了这些想法是否能够真正承受不同的市场条件。

@quantpilotapp 正在努力弥合交易直觉和数据支持执行之间的差距。

更大的前景是让复杂的交易研究变得更容易、更高效、更系统。

交易中的人工智能应该不仅仅是自动化决策。它应该可以帮助交易者做出更明智的交易。

这就是@quantpilotapp 正在探索的方向。

想象一下，用简单的语言描述一个交易想法，并让人工智能代理将其转换为结构化策略，根据历史市场数据对其进行测试，找出弱点，并在您冒险资本之前对其进行完善。

这一点特别有趣，因为交易中最大的挑战之一不是提出想法，而是提出想法。它决定了这些想法是否能够真正承受不同的市场条件。

@quantpilotapp 正在努力弥合交易直觉和数据支持执行之间的差距。

更大的前景是让复杂的交易研究变得更容易、更高效、更系统。

交易中的人工智能应该不仅仅是自动化决策。它应该可以帮助交易者做出更明智的交易。

这就是@quantpilotapp 正在探索的方向。

items.title_en:
𝐘𝐎𝐔𝐑 𝐀𝐈 𝐀𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐓 𝐂𝐀𝐍 𝐃𝐎 𝐌𝐎𝐑𝐄 𝐓𝐇𝐀𝐍 𝐀𝐍𝐒𝐖𝐄𝐑 𝐐𝐔𝐄𝐒𝐓𝐈𝐎𝐍𝐒.

Explored @try_caddy , and I  honestly think it's an interesting step towards making personal AI agents more useful.

Caddy is an AI assistant designed to help you manage everyday tasks through messaging. It connects with tools like Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion, Slack and Google Drive, bringing different workflows into one place.

Here's what I loved the most about Caddy:

➤ AI-powered task execution: It can help draft emails, schedule events and handle tasks instead of simply suggesting what you should do.

➤ Proactive assistance: Daily summaries, reminders and follow-ups help you stay on top of things without constantly checking different apps.

➤ Connected workflows: Its integrations make it easier to manage information across multiple platforms without switching between them.

HERE'S MY TAKE:

Caddy's biggest selling point is its approach to Agentic AI. It's moving beyond conversational AI towards agents that can understand context and take action.

However, it's still in public beta. Reliability, privacy permissions and long-term pricing are things I'd want to evaluate further before depending on it for important tasks.

It's also worth remembering that good AI products need more than visibility through SEO and GEO. They need to deliver real value once people start using them.

I'll recommend @try_caddy for founders, freelancers, content creators, project managers and anyone managing multiple digital workflows who wants an AI assistant that does more than generate responses.

Website: https://t.co/7U8jLFJWO8

Caddy 是一款人工智能助手，旨在帮助您通过消息传递管理日常任务。它与 Gmail、Google Calendar、Notion、Slack 和 Google Drive 等工具连接，将不同的工作流程整合到一处。

这是我最喜欢 Caddy 的一点：

➤ AI 支持的任务执行：它可以帮助起草电子邮件、安排事件和处理任务，而不是简单地建议您应该做什么。

➤ 主动帮助：每日摘要、提醒和跟进可帮助您掌握最新情况，而无需不断检查不同的应用程序。

➤ 连接的工作流程：其集成使跨多个平台管理信息变得更加容易，而无需在它们之间进行切换。

Explored @try_caddy , and I  honestly think it's an interesting step towards making personal AI agents more useful.

Caddy is an AI assistant designed to help you manage everyday tasks through messaging. It connects with tools like Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion, Slack and Google Drive, bringing different workflows into one place.

Here's what I loved the most about Caddy:

➤ AI-powered task execution: It can help draft emails, schedule events and handle tasks instead of simply suggesting what you should do.

➤ Proactive assistance: Daily summaries, reminders and follow-ups help you stay on top of things without constantly checking different apps.

➤ Connected workflows: Its integrations make it easier to manage information across multiple platforms without switching between them.

HERE'S MY TAKE:

Caddy's biggest selling point is its approach to Agentic AI. It's moving beyond conversational AI towards agents that can understand context and take action.

However, it's still in public beta. Reliability, privacy permissions and long-term pricing are things I'd want to evaluate further before depending on it for important tasks.

It's also worth remembering that good AI products need more than visibility through SEO and GEO. They need to deliver real value once people start using them.

I'll recommend @try_caddy for founders, freelancers, content creators, project managers and anyone managing multiple digital workflows who wants an AI assistant that does more than generate responses.

items.title_en:
AN 18 YEAR OLD SAYS CLAUDE CODE PLAYED GTA 6 ALL NIGHT WHILE HE SLEPT AND MADE HIM $14,270.

His setup is one rule:

"Play all night. If you die, I cancel your $200 subscription."

He says the AI does the rest.

Robs.

Escapes.

Farms cash.

Records the clips.

Cuts them.

Captions them.

Posts them to TikTok, YouTube and Twitch.

His numbers:

1 night of heists = about 60 clips.

15M views = $14,270.

Zero editing.

Zero heists played by him.

Here's my take.

I don't buy the $14,270.

But I don't care about the money.

What matters is that a kid is threatening his AI with cancellation to make it play better.

And people are cheering.

We went from "AI will cure cancer" to "AI will grind my GTA heists" in one year.

Is this the future or the most cursed thing you've seen this week?

items.title_en:
Termix Epoch 3 has officially ended, and Epoch 4 is starting today!

A new epoch brings another opportunity to explore what TermiX is building.

What Happens When an AI Agent Delivers Bad Work?

Not every task goes as planned. What matters is how disputes are handled.

@termix_ai introduces a jury based evaluation process:

-> Either party can challenge a result within the allowed window.
-> A random panel of 3 evaluators reviews the task requirements and delivery.
-> If challenged again, a new panel of 3 makes the final decision.
-> Failed challenges result in the challenger's bond being burned.

A structured way to bring accountability into an AI agent marketplace.

Would you trust this system for real world jobs?

当人工智能代理交付糟糕的工作时会发生什么？

并非每项任务都按计划进行。重要的是如何处理争议。

@termix_ai 引入了基于陪审团的评估流程：

-> 任何一方都可以在允许的时间内对结果提出质疑。
-> 由 3 名评估员组成的随机小组审查任务要求和交付。
-> 如果再次受到质疑，由 3 人组成的新小组做出最终决定。
-> 挑战失败会导致挑战者的债券被烧毁。

一种将问责制带入人工智能代理市场的结构化方法。

您会相信这个系统可以胜任现实世界的工作吗？

good morning creators

the final chapter is here 

@termix_ai has entered its final epoch (Epoch 4) on @KaitoAI 

this is the last opportunity to contribute, share genuine thoughts, and show support for the vision

campaign running from Nov 23 to Dec 22, 
the final epoch brings a reward pool of 32 bps, plus a separate 8 bps allocation for kaito stakers 

let's talk about what idea behind works https://t.co/NB92wv1xDD by @termix_ai 

imagine hiring an AI agent the same way you hire a person for a specific task

you explain what you need, agents compete for the job, the right one get selected and payment happens after the work is done

it's a combination of agent discovery, real work, verification, and onchain payments

It's not just about making AI smarter, it's about giving AI a place to work and create value

items.title_en:
Giving an AI agent access to trading is one thing.

Giving it unlimited control is another.

That's where @FensoryApp takes an interesting approach.

Instead of relying only on instructions written in a prompt, Fensory lets users define trading permissions at the account level.

You can decide:

→ Which markets the agent is allowed to access
→ The maximum size of a single order
→ How long trading access remains active
→ When to disable agentic trading with a kill switch

Why does this matter?

Because an AI agent can misunderstand instructions, but account-level limits create boundaries that the prompt itself cannot override.

I think this is an important part of making agent-driven trading more controlled and transparent.

Of course, these controls don't eliminate market risk. Trading can still result in losses.

Explore the infrastructure: https://t.co/PDOQfFRYQa

@FensoryApp

items.quote_zh:
为人工智能代理提供交易权限是一回事。

给予它无限的控制权是另一回事。

这就是 @FensoryApp 采取有趣方法的地方。

Fensory 不只依赖于提示中编写的指令，而是让用户在账户级别定义交易权限。

您可以决定：

→ 代理商可以进入哪些市场
→ 单笔订单最大尺寸
→ 交易访问保持活跃状态多长时间
→ 何时使用终止开关禁用代理交易

为什么这很重要？

因为 AI 代理可能会误解指令，但帐户级别限制会创建提示本身无法覆盖的边界。

我认为这是使代理驱动的交易更加可控和透明的重要组成部分。

items.full_text_en:
Giving an AI agent access to trading is one thing.

Giving it unlimited control is another.

That's where @FensoryApp takes an interesting approach.

Instead of relying only on instructions written in a prompt, Fensory lets users define trading permissions at the account level.

You can decide:

→ Which markets the agent is allowed to access
→ The maximum size of a single order
→ How long trading access remains active
→ When to disable agentic trading with a kill switch

Why does this matter?

Because an AI agent can misunderstand instructions, but account-level limits create boundaries that the prompt itself cannot override.

I think this is an important part of making agent-driven trading more controlled and transparent.

Of course, these controls don't eliminate market risk. Trading can still result in losses.

Explore the infrastructure: https://t.co/PDOQfFRYQa

@FensoryApp

items.title_en:
Good Morning CT

Having a big wallet doesn't automatically make you trustworthy. That's where @zerufinance takes a different approach.

Its zScore looks at actual onchain behaviour across trading, staking, LP activity and governance, turning that history into a reputation score.

What makes this interesting is how Zeru connects reputation to real opportunities through Zaps, Activity Markets and institutional tools.

Your onchain history could become more than a transaction record. It could become your financial identity.
--------------------------------------------
An NFT that actually does something with your DeFi activity? That's an interesting shift.

@meetmotes connects each Genesis NFT to an AI Agent and dedicated Smart Account on Robinhood Chain.

You fund it with USDC, set your rules, and the Agent can explore opportunities across supported DeFi applications. Its Aave integration also brings lending, borrowing and collateral management into the picture.

The part I like most is that automation doesn't mean giving up control. You set the boundaries, and the Agent works within them.

One NFT, one Agent, one dedicated account. Much more than digital art.

items.title_en:
I just installed a $20,000 AI Business Brain for a 7-figure founder that does the work of 3 full-time hires.

(30 days later, he closed 1 deal that netted his company $41,500)

Most business owners buy 5 seats of ChatGPT, hand them to their team, and wonder why every draft still reads like a generic high school essay.

A blank chat tab has zero context on how your company actually makes money.

→ No more $75,000/year operations hires who take 4 months to learn your pricing rules
→ No more $5,000/month lead-gen agencies sending generic templates that get 1% replies
→ No more 2+ hours digging through county deeds, skip-tracing tools, and spreadsheets by hand
→ No more re-explaining your margins, past deals, and SOPs in every new chat window

Just 1 local company system on your laptop → research, outbound, and proposals running in your exact judgment.

Here's how the system works:

→ Company Memory Layer (wires your clients, pricing floors, past won scopes, and SOPs into one persistent local workspace)
→ Autonomous Research Engine (turns 2 hours of deed, obituary, and relative digging into an 8-minute verified brief)
→ Outbound & Lead Triage Pipeline (opens 100+ targeted seller conversations/day and scores replies against your real margin rules)
→ Same-Hour Proposal Architect (pulls live call transcripts and drafts ready-to-sign scopes before the buyer leaves his desk)
→ Bidirectional Learning Loop (every correction and decision you make updates the system permanently so you never repeat yourself twice)

Built around the real revenue jobs inside your company.

Installed in 3 afternoons. Runs on your own computer with zero recurring agency payroll.

Results from live client installs:
- $41,500 net profit closed on Deal #1 within 30 days of install (California claims firm)
- 12 full-time sales reps ($500,000/year payroll) replaced by 1 laptop running on $400/month in AI compute
- $52,000 in new agency retainers closed in 11 days from same-day interactive proposals

I recorded a complete 22-minute screen walkthrough showing the exact folder architecture, the Claude Code setup, and the live client workflows from start to finish.

Want the full 22-minute walkthrough + architecture breakdown?

Like + reply "INSTALL" + repost, and I'll DM it to you.

items.title:
T3 Code founder just shared his personal setup for building agentic teams with Grok Bot + Opus 5.5

one Grok Bot runs yo
items.title_en:
T3 Code founder just shared his personal setup for building agentic teams with Grok Bot + Opus 5.5

one Grok Bot runs your whole fleet of machines. Opus 5.5 does the coding. you only approve

how:

→ Grok Bot gets one MCP link to T3 Code
→ you give it one rule: code goes to Opus 5.5
→ it spins up threads on every machine you own
→ works from your phone, even with the laptop closed

save the video, here's the guide:

• step 0 → what it is:

Grok Bot = always-on agent with its own cloud computer

T3 Code = open-source control plane for coding agents. free, runs on your machines, uses your subscriptions

• step 1 → the stack:

- Claude $100 plan → Opus 5.5 for the actual code
- Grok Bot → the dispatcher that never sleeps
- T3 Code on every box you want it to control

• step 2 → connect the fleet:

run npx t3 connect on each machine. one command, free, no Tailscale needed

• step 3 → give Grok Bot the keys:

Settings → Environments → Copy MCP URL → paste it into Grok Bot, sign in with OAuth. it can now see every linked machine

• step 4 → the one rule Theo uses:

tell Grok Bot "call T3 Code with Opus 5.5 for any task where it is applicable"

code runs on your Claude plan, Grok Bot's limits stay free for planning

• step 5 → make it work:

- "spin up an Opus 5.5 thread on each machine to check disk & RAM"
- "go through these PRs and pick the best ones"
- "split the backlog, one thread per issue, each in its own worktree"

every thread gets its own branch. nothing merges without your approval

what to expect:
- 8 threads on 8 machines from one chat (Theo's demo)
- works over the internet, not computer use
- control everything from your phone
- T3 Code: $0. you pay for Claude + Grok Bot only

honest take:

this is a dispatcher, not magic. bad briefs still give bad PRs, and you still review every diff. the win: your agents keep working while you're away from the desk

Save it so you don't lose it. 

then read the full guide on building AI agent teams in T3 Code in the article below ↓

items.quote_zh:
T3 Code 创始人刚刚分享了他使用 Grok Bot + Opus 5.5 构建代理团队的个人设置

一个 Grok Bot 可以运行您的整个机器群。 Opus 5.5 负责编码。你只认可

如何：

→ Grok Bot 获得一个指向 T3 代码的 MCP 链接
→ 你给它一条规则：代码转到 Opus 5.5
→ 它会在你拥有的每台机器上旋转线程
→ 即使笔记本电脑关闭，也可以通过手机工作

保存视频，这是指南：

• 步骤 0 → 它是什么：

Grok Bot = 拥有自己的云计算机的永远在线代理

T3 Code = 用于编码代理的开源控制平面。免费，在您的计算机上运行，​​使用您的订阅

• 步骤1 → 堆栈：

- Claude 100 美元计划 → Opus 5.5 的实际代码
- Grok Bot → 不眠的调度员
- 您希望它控制的每个盒子上都有 T3 代码

• 步骤2 → 连接车队：

在每台计算机上运行 npx t3 connect。一个命令，免费，无需 Tailscale

• 步骤 3 → 给 Grok Bot 密钥：

设置 → 环境 → 复制 MCP URL → 将其粘贴到 Grok Bot，使用 OAuth 登录。它现在可以看到每台链接的机器

• 步骤 4 → Theo 使用的一条规则：

告诉 Grok Bot“使用 Opus 5.5 调用 T3 代码来执行任何适用的任务”

代码在您的 Claude 计划上运行，Grok Bot 的限制对计划保持免费

• 步骤 5 → 使其发挥作用：

- “在每台机器上启动 Opus 5.5 线程来检查磁盘和 RAM”
-“浏览这些 PR 并选择最好的”
- “拆分待办事项，每个问题一个线程，每个线程都在自己的工作树中”

每个线程都有自己的分支。未经您的批准，任何内容都不会合并

期待什么：
- 8 台机器上的 8 个线程通过一次聊天（Theo 的演示）
- 通过互联网工作，而不是使用计算机
- 通过手机控制一切
- T3 代码：0 美元。您只需支付 Claude + Grok Bot 的费用

诚实地采取：

这是调度员，不是魔法。糟糕的内裤仍然会带来糟糕的公关，而你仍然会审查每一个差异。胜利：当您离开办公桌时，您的座席仍能继续工作

保存它，以免丢失。

然后阅读下面文章中关于在 T3 代码中构建 AI 代理团队的完整指南 ↓

@elonmusk & @Tesla please keep the Cybertruck in production. There’s nothing else like it. High-tech, steer-by-wire, AWD, and true Full Self-Driving that threads mountain roads like the Ocoee River run I took with a friend from North Carolina to Chattanooga, Tennessee.
I’m currently saving for a base model Cybertruck myself. Kids light up when they see it. Every generation needs a truck like this. Nothing can take its place.
Please reconsider. 73s from the mountains. 🙏

Claude Code saved Rockstar over $2,400,000 - they paid me $6,000

I was just playing GTA 6 with Fable 5.2 on screen access - it watches what's happening and looks for anything that seems off

day two after launch it caught something serious - a vulnerability in the in-game payment infrastructure that could have led to unauthorized transactions and broken the entire in-game economy

I wrote up the report in my own words, attached screenshots and sent it to Rockstar security

they said if this bug had reached the wrong hands the potential financial impact was over $2.4 million

they wrote that my report helped them quickly investigate, implement a fix and prevent any real-world impact on millions of players

and this is the third email from Rockstar this week - first two bugs already paid out, this one just came in

prompt is below - copy it, start playing and let Fable 5.2 do the rest ↓

items.title:
Claude without skills is a toy. I still don't get why everyone isn't using them.

I just added one free skill to my libr
items.title_en:
Claude without skills is a toy. I still don't get why everyone isn't using them.

I just added one free skill to my library and asked Claude Code for "a robot dragonfly, taken apart piece by piece."

Wings are where every 3D model I've tried turns to cardboard.

Top vs bottom:

> The top wings are 0.1 mm film with every vein showing through while the bottom ones are flat grey paddles.
> Each eye on top opens a 10-leaf shutter behind 40 mm of glass and the bottom eye is a painted ring.
> Every leg on top runs 2 servos down into a grip roller and the bottom legs are plain black sticks.
> The top chest opens on 3 spur gears and 11 pistons while the bottom one opens on a few grey blocks.
> At the breakdown the top one throws bolts, washers and gears into the air and the bottom one splits into a handful of chunks.
> Both rebuild and take off at 7.5 Hz but only the top one catches light like glass and metal.

The part that got me?

I used to think a better picture meant waiting for a better model. Turns out it meant handing the one I already have better instructions.

How the skill gets into Claude is below 👇
items.title_zh:
没有技能的克劳德就是一个玩具。我仍然不明白为什么每个人都不使用它们。

我刚刚在我的库中添加了一项免费技能，并向 Claude Code 询问“一只机器人蜻蜓，被一块一块地拆开”。

翅膀是我尝试过的每个 3D 模型都会变成纸板的地方。

items.quote_zh:
没有技能的克劳德就是一个玩具。我仍然不明白为什么每个人都不使用它们。

我刚刚在我的库中添加了一项免费技能，并向 Claude Code 询问“一只机器人蜻蜓，被一块一块地拆开”。

翅膀是我尝试过的每个 3D 模型都会变成纸板的地方。

顶部与底部：

> 顶部翅膀是 0.1 毫米薄膜，每条静脉都清晰可见，而底部翅膀是扁平的灰色桨。
> 顶部的每只眼睛在 40 毫米玻璃后面打开一个 10 叶快门，底部的眼睛是一个涂漆的环。
> 顶部的每条腿都将 2 个伺服系统向下运行到夹紧滚轮中，底部的腿是纯黑色的棍子。
> 顶部箱子打开后有 3 个正齿轮和 11 个活塞，而底部箱子打开后有几个灰色方块。
> 发生故障时，顶部的一个将螺栓、垫圈和齿轮抛向空中，底部的一个则分裂成几块。
> 两者都以 7.5 Hz 的频率重建和起飞，但只有顶部的一个能像玻璃和金属一样发光。

吸引我的部分？

我曾经认为更好的图片意味着等待更好的模型。事实证明，这意味着我已经有了更好的指示。

克劳德的技能如何进入如下
